Each puzzle provides only one to three black-and-white line drawings and a minimal submission instruction, requiring agents to discover the underlying solving mechanism entirely from the images. Across 29 reasoning-effort configurations of eight frontier models, even the strongest model, GPT-6 Astra (max), achieves only 26.7% accuracy, while five of the eight models score below 1%. Yet on a ten-task subset, providing a single non-spoiler mechanism hint boosts accuracy from 12.2% to 51.1%. This sharp contrast shows that the primary bottleneck of current agents lies not in executing multi-step plans, but in autonomously discovering rules from visual evidence. Visual Cipher Bench thus provides a rigorous benchmark for measuring long-horizon visual reasoning in agents.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Haofeng Wang, Xuanyi Liu, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: PhysCapBench is a novel benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, assessing annotation quality across diverse domains to enhance physical AI training and performance.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Yuhan Tang, Ke Fan, Xinkai Zou, Baichuan Mo, Kangxin Cui
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper introduces Ask2Decide, a benchmark assessing LLM agents' ability to acquire crucial decision-relevant information from humans, revealing significant challenges in planning accuracy.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: Ego-CEVR is a framework that enhances robot learning by leveraging egocentric videos through distinct global and interaction representation objectives, achieving superior performance and generalization.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Egocentric videos offer a low-cost, scalable source of manipulation experience for robot learning. However, existing methods often fail to tailor their use of egocentric videos and robot demonstrations to the differences in their formats and information content. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns task context through future video prediction, while the interaction module uses this context to interpret wrist observations and learns local execution information through robot action supervision. The distinct learning objectives enable independent pretraining on large-scale human and robot egocentric videos to learn task context, and training on real-robot demonstrations to align the learned representations with fine-grained robot actions. Experiments show leading performance on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, while real-robot evaluations demonstrate generalization across tasks and embodiments.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Non-Imaging Optical Tactile Sensors for Robotics: Transduction Principles, System Integration, and Robotic Applications
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Hao Wu, Yu Feng, Haotian Guo, Huichan Zhao, Changsheng Wu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: This review explores non-imaging optical tactile sensors in robotics, emphasizing their design, integration, and performance in accurately detecting contact variables amidst mechanical influences.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Non-imaging optical tactile sensors encode contact through changes in optical intensity, wavelength, spectra, or photon counts, offering diverse architectures for robotic touch. Their usefulness depends on whether contact variables can be reliably distinguished from coupled mechanical and environmental effects, and whether the resulting information can be delivered in time to guide action. This review develops a unified framework linking mechanical load transmission, optical encoding, readout, and tactile inference to robotic task requirements. It examines reflective and waveguide-based devices, micro/nanofibers, fiber gratings, interferometric and resonant structures, and mechanoluminescent composites. Three considerations emerge across these approaches. First, high optical sensitivity supports accurate tactile estimation only when target variables remain identifiable under the relevant contact and calibration conditions. Second, spatial coverage and feedback timing must be assessed at the system level, accounting for multiplexing, acquisition, demodulation, and inference. Third, device characterization, offline recognition, and closed-loop robotic performance provide distinct levels of evidence and require different evaluation criteria. Representative studies illustrate how these considerations shape force estimation, contact localization, slip correction and distributed interaction. This review concludes with priorities for calibration transfer, reliable interfaces, scalable readout, and task-based validation, providing a basis for selecting and developing non-imaging optical tactile architectures for robotics.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: ExtremeDrive: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Critical Driving
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Xinhan Li, Yuhong Jiang, Shiyue Zhao, Junzhi Zhang, Chengkun He
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: ExtremeDrive is a comprehensive dataset and benchmark for autonomous driving, focusing on safety-critical scenarios and extreme conditions, enhancing trajectory prediction and driving performance.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Existing autonomous driving datasets and benchmarks provide extensive resources for routine driving, yet real-world data covering safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions remain limited. To address this gap, we present ExtremeDrive, a real-world dataset and benchmark covering emergency maneuvers, complex traffic interactions, and adverse conditions such as slippery or snow-covered roads, alongside routine driving. The dataset comprises 589 driving scenes curated from a larger pool of real-world driving recordings, with calibrated and aligned multisensor data and reviewed annotations of road structure and traffic participants. We further establish a benchmark to evaluate planned trajectories through simulated vehicle execution, measuring safety-related metrics and driving performance. Experiments at equal training set sizes show that incorporating critical driving data reduces trajectory prediction errors and improves mean critical-success rates in critical scenarios. ExtremeDrive provides a unified resource for learning and evaluating autonomous driving in safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: AsymEEF: Bimanual Manipulation with Asymmetric End Effectors
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Xiaokang Sun, Ningyue Wang, Kunqi Xu, Guangqi Jiang, Jianglong Ye
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: AsymEEF enables efficient bimanual manipulation by transferring demonstrations across diverse end-effectors, enhancing policy learning and execution success without additional teleoperation.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Teleoperated demonstrations are costly to collect and rarely reusable across end-effectors with different kinematics and action spaces. This burden grows in bimanual manipulation, where each end-effector pair may require new data. We present AsymEEF, a framework for executable cross-end-effector demonstration generation and unified bimanual policy learning. Given a small source dataset, AsymEEF transfers demonstrations to heterogeneous combinations of two-, three-, and five-fingered end-effectors without additional teleoperation. Kinematic teacher anchors provide geometric supervision, while sparse real-world X-Calib anchors correct discrepancies in grasp execution. A shared encoder maps wrist poses and actuator states to a morphology-agnostic latent space, and a morphology-conditioned decoder reconstructs target commands. Generated trajectories undergo replay filtering for task-level executability. The representation also supports a unified bimanual visuomotor policy trained across multiple pairs. Across four simulated and six real-world tasks, AsymEEF improves replay success over adapted transfer baselines, achieves a mean replay-valid expansion gain of 16.6 times in simulation, and is evaluated through downstream policy training on real robots. Project website: https://asymeef.vercel.app/.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: ReRead: Wrong Predictions, Useful Representations - Correcting Frozen Robot Policies by Re-reading Their Own Representations
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Xu Su, Shunlong Xiao, Qintao Yi, Mingkuan Zhao, Xinmiao Yu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The ReRead method enhances frozen robot policies by correcting action predictions using past representations, improving success rates significantly across various tasks without additional visual encoders.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: When a pretrained robot policy fails on challenging tasks, common remedies include retraining the backbone, adding an external visual encoder, or introducing a memory module. We argue that wrong predictions do not imply wrong representations: a policy can retain the required information yet fail to read it out as the correct action. To test this view, we propose ReRead: with the backbone frozen, a corrector re-reads the current and two previous caches to predict an action residual. The corrector sees no images, is trained solely on offline demonstrations from all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and adds only 4.17% latency. Ablations and interventions show that the correction relies on the backbone's own representations: none of four external visual encoders adds further gain, and swapping in past caches from other trajectories sharply increases action error. On the 11 hardest RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, ReRead improves the success rates of LingBot-VLA, $π_{0.5}$, and Fast-WAM by 23.45, 13.09, and 8.00 percentage points, respectively. In paired evaluation on all 50 tasks, it raises Fast-WAM's average success rate from 90.73% to 92.66%. On a Flexiv dual-arm robot, it raises success on a phase-ambiguous task from 0% to 36%.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: ODEWorld: A Continuous Predictive Architecture via Physical-Time Flow
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Dongxiu Liu, Haoyi Niu, Peng Cheng, Yuan Gao, Xirui Kang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: ODEWorld introduces a continuous predictive architecture using Physical-Time Flow and ODEs to enhance efficiency in modeling dynamics, enabling high-quality predictions and planning in robotics.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: In the physical world we inhabit, space and time are fundamentally continuous. However, existing machine learning paradigms for world modeling are largely confined to discrete-time prediction, thereby exhibiting significant inefficiency in capturing the dynamics of physical world. We introduce Physical-Time Flow (PT-Flow), a novel approach that learns a continuous latent velocity field operating in physical time. Crucially, the underlying dynamics of sequential data are parameterized by an ordinary differential equation (ODE) embedded in a well-structured representation space. Under this paradigm, the prediction of future can be recast as temporal integration via an ODE solver in the compressed latent space. Building upon PT-Flow, we construct ODEWorld, a continuous-time latent world model that is both efficient and versatile. By extracting time-variant features and enforcing ODE properties on both the dynamical representation space and the latent velocity field, ODEWorld effectively addresses the long-standing representation collapse issue in latent world model literature. This also enables high-quality image reconstruction even after long-horizon prediction. Moreover, its continuous nature allows for arbitrary temporal resolution and even backward prediction, which is impossible for most discrete-time models. Lastly, ODEWorld can provide rich planning-oriented information to facilitate downstream policy learning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that ODEWorld successfully reconciles planning-conducive dynamics abstraction with visual realism, excelling in both video generation and robotic control. Project page: https://dstate.github.io/odeworld_website/.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: OA-WAM: Object-Addressable World Action Model for Robust Robot Manipulation
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Yushan Liu, Peibo Sun, Shoujie Li, Yifan Xie, Lingfeng Zhang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: OA-WAM introduces an object-addressable world action model that enhances robot manipulation robustness across varying conditions, achieving superior performance in multiple benchmarks and real-robot tasks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) learn manipulation by predicting actions and future observations, yet their success drops sharply when the camera viewpoint, object layout or robot initial state changes. Such changes keep the instructed object the same but alter the appearance and pose features the policy observes, which in standard attention also form the keys that locate the object. We introduce OA-WAM, an object-addressable WAM that finds each object by an identity address fixed for the episode and reads its changing state. In every layer of a pretrained multimodal trunk, object-slot keys depend only on the address and frame position, and values carry the current state; the same addresses key the action pointer and index per-object forecasts, which can trigger re-grounding. Fine-tuned on standard LIBERO demonstrations, OA-WAM transfers zero-shot to LIBERO-Plus with 90.5% success, outperforming all ten published baselines. It also leads on LIBERO (99.0%) and, fine-tuned on BridgeData V2, on SimplerEnv WidowX (88.9%). On five real-robot tasks, it succeeds in 89 of 100 nominal trials, versus 73 for the strongest baseline. Ablations trace its robustness to addressing rather than to object slots: with standard attention, slots do no better than a slot-free policy, and addressing them by identity raises geometric success by 10.7 points. Forecasting the addressed objects is likewise a stronger training signal than forecasting image codes.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: EgoEMG: A Multimodal Egocentric Dataset with Bilateral EMG and Vision for Hand Pose Estimation
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Ziheng Xi, Jiayi Yu, Yanbo Duan, Yitao Wang, Jinyang Yu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: EgoEMG introduces a multimodal dataset combining bilateral sEMG and egocentric video for improved hand pose estimation, achieving notable accuracy enhancements through feature fusion.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Hand pose estimation from egocentric video is challenging under adverse visual conditions, such as occlusion. Wrist-worn surface electromyography (sEMG) measures muscle activity without requiring visual access to the hand, offering a wearable complement to egocentric cameras. Evaluating their combined use requires synchronized physiological and visual recordings with continuous pose annotations, which existing EMG-based hand pose datasets do not jointly provide. We introduce EgoEMG, a multimodal dataset pairing bilateral wrist sEMG with egocentric video and motion-capture-derived hand poses, supplemented by external multi-view RGB-D recordings. EgoEMG contains 25.9 hours of recordings from 68 participants, covering 60 bare-hand gesture classes and interactions with 10 everyday objects. We establish EMG-only, vision-only, and fusion benchmarks with shared 22-dimensional pose targets and evaluations on unseen users, gestures, and objects. For EMG-only estimation, EMGFormer achieves the lowest overall MAE among the compared methods on EgoEMG and competitive results on EMG2Pose. Our residual fusion model combines ViT and EMGFormer features. Adding EMG reduces error for both single-frame and temporal vision models, with MAE decreasing from $7.39^\circ$ to $7.06^\circ$ for ViT-L. The largest absolute reduction occurs when evaluating interactions with an unseen object. Generalization to unseen users remains challenging. Project page: https://zhenqis123.github.io/egoemg-site/.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Beyond Visual Cues: Semantic-Driven Token Filtering and Expert Routing for Anytime Person ReID
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Jiaxuan Li, Xin Wen, Zhihang Li
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper presents STFER, a framework utilizing Large Vision-Language Models for robust person re-identification across varying conditions by integrating semantic-driven filtering and expert routing.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Any-Time Person Re-identification (AT-ReID) necessitates the robust retrieval of target individuals under arbitrary conditions, encompassing both modality shifts (daytime and nighttime) and extensive clothing-change scenarios, ranging from short-term to long-term intervals. However, existing methods are highly relying on pure visual features, which are prone to change due to environmental and time factors, resulting in significantly performance deterioration under scenarios involving illumination caused modality shifts or cloth-change. In this paper, we propose Semantic-driven Token Filtering and Expert Routing (STFER), a novel framework that leverages the ability of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to generate identity consistency text, which provides identity-discriminative features that are robust to both clothing variations and cross-modality shifts between RGB and IR. Specifically, we employ instructions to guide the LVLM in generating identity-intrinsic semantic text that captures biometric constants for the semantic model driven. The text token is further used for Semantic-driven Visual Token Filtering (SVTF), which enhances informative visual regions and suppresses redundant background noise. Meanwhile, the text token is also used for Semantic-driven Expert Routing (SER), which integrates the semantic text into expert routing, resulting in more robust multi-scenario gating. Extensive experiments on the Any-Time ReID dataset (AT-USTC) demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art results. Moreover, the model trained on AT-USTC was evaluated across 5 widely-used ReID benchmarks demonstrating superior generalization capabilities with highly competitive results. Our code will be available soon.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: PlanDiv: Test-Time Scaling with Latent Plans for Vision-Language-Action Models
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Hanbo Zhang, Lianlei Shan, Liuhaichen Yang, Zezhi Tang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: PlanDiv enhances vision-language-action models by generating diverse action candidates through latent plans, significantly improving task success rates compared to traditional resampling methods.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Test-time scaling improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies by drawing several action candidates and executing the best one. We find that its returns diminish quickly when the candidates are resampled from one decoder: they differ by noise rather than by plan, and for each of three resampling sources, going from four to eight candidates adds only 0.06-0.07 to the average number of completed tasks on CALVIN. We introduce PlanDiv, an action head that makes the candidates differ by plan: a lightweight planner proposes K latent plan hypotheses, a shared masked-diffusion executor decodes one action chunk per plan from a single backbone pass, and the policy executes the chunk that its own likelihood ranks highest. The plans are learned from demonstrations alone, without plan labels or rewards. With the backbone, data and training recipe held fixed, eight plan-conditioned candidates raise five-task chain success on CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D from 56.9% to 69.9%, while eight candidates from autoregressive, plan-free or same-plan resampling reach at most 64.9%. The same-plan baseline is PlanDiv's own checkpoint with the plan held fixed, so this gap comes from the plans, not from drawing more samples. On LIBERO-Long, four plans remove 40% of single-candidate failures, against at most 21% for matched resampling. On a real Franka arm the gain appears where a task admits more than one solution: PlanDiv is on par with a single-output OpenVLA-OFT+ baseline on a one-solution task and succeeds in 51 of 54 trials against 40 of 54 on two tasks with two solutions.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Beyond Vehicle-Centric Data: Scaling Autonomous Driving through Roadside-to-Vehicle Generation
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Yichen Zhang, Zihan Wang, Hao Chen, Runyi Huang, Ruixue Zong
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The AnyR2V framework transforms roadside traffic data into diverse vehicle-centric training videos, enhancing autonomous driving model performance by generating multi-perspective datasets.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Training autonomous driving models requires large and diverse datasets, collected primarily by vehicles. Scaling them entails investment in fleet operation, data processing and annotation. Road infrastructure records traffic and multi-vehicle interactions, yet the viewpoint gap between roadside and onboard sensors limits its direct use for training. Here we introduce AnyR2V, a framework that transforms multimodal roadside observations into seven-camera surround-view videos for different vehicle perspectives. It aggregates sequential observations into a shared scene representation of geometry and road-user motion, then renders appearance, depth and layout conditions along target-vehicle trajectories. Supervised by spatiotemporally aligned roadside-vehicle pairs, AnyR2V generates surround-view videos guided by scene structure and road-user motion. Existing roadside 3D bounding boxes are transformed into target-vehicle coordinates and paired with generated images, allowing one traffic recording and its annotations to yield training data from multiple vehicle perspectives. We construct R2V360, a dataset of 89 real traffic sequences at an urban intersection, with aligned multimodal roadside data and onboard surround-view videos. AnyR2V outperforms six scene reconstruction methods in image fidelity and in depth and semantic agreement between generated and real onboard images. We further evaluate generated videos along other vehicles' trajectories by adding them to real training data. Adding generated frames equal to 50% of the original real training frame count improves mean average precision (mAP) by 3.3-3.4 AP-points across three 3D object detectors on the real onboard test set, relative to real-data-only baselines. These results demonstrate that roadside traffic records can provide training data from multiple vehicle perspectives, offering a new data source for autonomous driving.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: M-CROSS: A Multisensor Simulation Dataset for SLAM across Water--Land Transitions
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Yan Dong, Tianyi Wu, Junyu Yang, Shaoqiang Qiu, Zefeng Yan
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: M-CROSS is a novel multisensor simulation dataset for SLAM, addressing localization challenges in water-land transitions with new metrics and demonstrating existing methods' inadequacies.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Water--land cross-domain robots require continuous localization across land, transition and underwater phases, where sensor characteristics and availability change abruptly. Existing datasets and conventional metrics are not designed to capture transition-induced degradation and failures. We present \textbf{M-CROSS}, to the best of our knowledge, the first multisensor simulation dataset and benchmark for SLAM across continuous water--land transitions. It provides synchronized LiDAR, sonar, stereo camera, IMU, DVL, and depth measurements; 6DoF pose ground truth; sensor-wise medium-state annotations; and medium-dependent sensor degradation models. We establish a transition-aware protocol comprising the Trajectory Completion Rate (TCR), Piecewise Absolute Pose Error (PW-APE), Transition End Error (TEE), and Transition Survival Period (TSP), which measure trajectory completion, single-domain accuracy, transition-induced error, and localization survival under prolonged partial immersion, respectively. Experiments with 6 representative SLAM systems show that existing methods fail to maintain both localization accuracy and trajectory continuity across the full set of water--land transitions, exhibiting transition-induced drift, trajectory discontinuities, and tracking failures. M-CROSS is publicly available https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MCross-Dataset

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Kuan Zhang, Zirong Chen
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: RISE-RL enhances open-ended reinforcement learning by selectively exploring trajectories based on missed rubric criteria, significantly improving performance across various benchmarks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) for open-ended tasks is challenging because responses must satisfy multidimensional criteria without following a single correct generation trajectory. Existing rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) methods compress fine-grained criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards, making persistent capability gaps difficult to target under limited on-policy exploration. We propose $\textbf{RISE-RL}$ (Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration), which uses repeatedly missed rubric criteria to elicit privileged trajectories that are difficult to discover through unguided exploration alone. RISE-RL retains only trajectories whose complete-rubric reward exceeds the mean reward of natural rollouts, and then re-evaluates them under the original prompt to emphasize behaviors that remain weakly supported by the natural policy. The resulting guidance signal is optimized through a separate auxiliary objective and removed once its additional benefit diminishes. Experiments with 4B and 14B models across writing, chat, health, and science show that RISE-RL achieves the highest mean score on every evaluated benchmark under guidance-free evaluation. Compared with standard Rubric-RL, it improves the average score by 1.3 points at the 4B scale and $\textbf{3.3 points at the 14B scale}$, including a $\textbf{6.0-point}$ gain on CreativeWriting-V3. It also improves creative-writing diversity and yields gains on objectively scored medical and scientific benchmarks. These results indicate that selective internalization through reward filtering and policy support shaping is effective for open-ended reinforcement learning.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: LatentUM: Unleashing the Potential of Interleaved Cross-Modal Reasoning via a Latent-Space Unified Model
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Jiachun Jin, Zetong Zhou, Xiao Yang, Hao Zhang, Pengfei Liu
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: LatentUM introduces a unified model that enhances interleaved cross-modal reasoning by utilizing a shared semantic latent space, achieving state-of-the-art performance in visual tasks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Unified models (UMs) hold promise for their ability to understand and generate content across heterogeneous modalities. Compared to merely generating visual content, the use of UMs for interleaved cross-modal reasoning is more promising and valuable, e.g., for solving understanding problems that require dense visual thinking, improving visual generation through self-reflection, or modeling visual dynamics of the physical world guided by stepwise action interventions. However, existing UMs typically rely on pixel decoding as a bridge when their visual representations for understanding and generation are disjoint, which is both ineffective and computationally cumbersome. In this paper, we introduce LatentUM, a novel unified model that represents all modalities within a shared semantic latent space, eliminating pixel-space mediation for model-internal reasoning over generated visual states. By making generated visual tokens directly interpretable to the model itself, LatentUM enables flexible interleaved cross-modal reasoning and generation. Empirically, LatentUM achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Visual Spatial Planning benchmark, pushes the limits of visual generation through self-reflection and demonstrates world modeling capability by predicting future visual states in the shared semantic latent space. Code and models are available at https://github.com/SJTU-DENG-Lab/LatentUM.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: USER: A Unified and Extensible System for Online Real-World Policy Learning in Embodied AI
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Hongzhi Zang, Shu'ang Yu, Hao Lin, Tianxing Zhou, Zefang Huang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: USER is a unified system that enhances online real-world policy learning in embodied AI through hardware abstraction, adaptive communication, and asynchronous training frameworks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Online policy learning directly in the physical world is a promising yet challenging direction for embodied intelligence. Unlike simulation, real-world systems cannot be arbitrarily accelerated, cheaply reset, or massively replicated, suggesting that real-world policy learning is not merely an algorithmic problem, but inherently a systems problem. We present \user, a \underline{U}nified and extensible \underline{S}yst\underline{E}m for online real-world policy lea\underline{R}ning. On the systems side, \user introduces a hardware abstraction layer for unified robot management and an adaptive communication plane that enables efficient cloud-edge training. On the learning side, \user adopts a fully asynchronous training framework, designs a persistent and cache-aware replay buffer, and provides extensible abstractions for rewards, algorithms, and policies. Experiments in both simulation and the real world demonstrate that \user supports multi-robot coordination, heterogeneous manipulators, cloud-edge training with large models, and long-running asynchronous training. Together, these capabilities establish \user as a unified and extensible systems foundation for online real-world policy learning.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: ReST-RL: Reinforcing LLM Reasoning through Unified Self-Training and Value-Guided Search
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Sining Zhoubian, Dan Zhang, Jie Tang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: ReST-RL enhances LLM reasoning accuracy through a unified self-training and value-guided search framework, outperforming existing reinforcement learning and decoding methods across various benchmarks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: With respect to improving the reasoning accuracy of LLMs, the representative reinforcement learning (RL) method - Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) - has achieved critical success, yet it still suffers from the issue of insignificant reward signals. This paper introduces ReST-RL, a unified Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) policy-value framework that reconnects policy optimization and value-guided search to improve LLM reasoning ability. Firstly, ReST-GRPO adopts an optimized ReST-style algorithm to reshape the policy-induced trajectory distribution by increasing the reward variance of GRPO sampling and exposing the policy to more informative partial states, thereby improving training efficiency and effectiveness. Then, we further introduce a decoding optimization method, VM-MCTS, which trains a Value Model (VM) from self-collected Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) targets and deploys it through an adapted MCTS algorithm to provide precise process signals and verification scores, further enhancing reasoning accuracy. These two stages are internally dependent - ReST-GRPO yields higher quality trajectories for value learning with VM-MCTS, which in turn enables more effective inference-time search. We validate our framework on multiple coding benchmarks (e.g., APPS, BigCodeBench, and HumanEval), where it significantly outperforms other reinforcement training baselines (naive GRPO, DAPO, and ReST-DPO), as well as decoding and verification baselines (e.g., PRM-BoN and ORM-MCTS), indicating its power to strengthen LLM reasoning capability. Moreover, we further evaluate ReST-RL on out-of-domain math and science reasoning tasks, where it achieves improved performance without target-domain tuning and favorable end-to-end efficiency trade-offs, providing preliminary transfer evidence beyond our primary coding domain.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: SARGO: Agreement-Gated Reinforcement and Suppression via On-Policy Self-Guidance for Visual Hallucination Mitigation
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Jinyu Li, Zhiming Zhang, Hao Fang, Hongyao Yu, Bin Chen
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: SARGO introduces a post-training framework that selectively reinforces accurate visual information while mitigating hallucinations in vision-language models through on-policy self-guidance.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language models remain susceptible to visual hallucinations, often mixing grounded information with unsupported claims in the same response. Response-level reinforcement learning assigns a shared advantage to all tokens in a response, causing negative updates to suppress correct information alongside unsupported claims. To reduce hallucination while preserving useful visual information, we introduce SARGO (Self-guided Advantage-Routed Grounding Optimization), a post-training framework for selective reinforcement and suppression through on-policy self-guidance. Direct and reciprocal weighting gives better-supported tokens stronger reinforcement on positive updates and weaker penalties on negative updates. Agreement between overall and hallucination-specific advantages selects when to apply this guidance. At the response level, a reference-calibrated reward couples factuality with the retention and expansion of grounded information, discouraging lower hallucination scores obtained through omission. Experiments on Qwen3-VL-4B, Qwen3-VL-8B, and Gemma3-4B demonstrate that SARGO outperforms the evaluated mitigation baselines across Obj-Hal, AMBER, THRONE, and SHR evaluations. SARGO achieves these gains while preserving useful visual information and general multimodal capabilities.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Yuan Wei, Ying Wei
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper explores how on-policy distillation reshapes interaction patterns in language-model agents across various domains, revealing both improvements and negative transfers in performance.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Guangzhi Sun, Zhonghao Zhai, Yixuan Li, Chao Zhang
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The VEX framework enhances computer-use agents by leveraging audio-visual understanding from tutorial videos for improved task execution and self-verification, achieving significant performance gains.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior. Following a watch-act-rewatch paradigm, the agent extracts procedural guidance from tutorial videos containing visual demonstrations and spoken explanations, executes tasks, and verifies its progress by rewatching its execution as video. We instantiate VEX with video-SALMONN-VEX, a 9B-scale audio-visual computer-use agent built on the video-SALMONN 2 architecture with a Qwen3.5-9B backbone. We further introduce Action-Grounded Guide Optimization (AGGO), a reinforcement learning method that optimizes video-derived guidance for downstream action prediction, and augment AgentNet, OSWorld, and CUA-Gym with over 24K real-world tutorial videos. Experiments on OSWorld and a complementary subset of CUA-Gym demonstrate consistent improvements, with video-SALMONN-VEX achieving a 22% relative increase in task success over its Qwen3.5 backbone on OSWorld. Moreover, its generated guidance improves Gemini-3.5-flash by 10% relatively on OSWorld. These results highlight the potential of audio-visual understanding as a unified interface for procedural learning and self-verification in computer-use agents.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: Recognizing Events Is Not Enough: Why Streaming VLMs Struggle in Compositional Instruction Triggering
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Yehua Huang, Penglei Sun, Xiang Li, Jinhao Zhou, Jiawen Wen
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: The paper introduces TEMPI, a real-time VLM agent that improves compositional instruction execution in streaming video by effectively managing temporal constraints and task progress.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Recognizing individual events does not guarantee correct execution of compositional instructions in streaming video. For example, given the request "Notify me when the pot boils after someone turns on the stove and leaves the kitchen", existing models may recognize the individual events yet notify too early or miss the intended moment, failing to track how their temporal conditions are satisfied over time. To evaluate this gap, we introduce CoTriggerBench, which composes annotated video events into temporally constrained instructions and verifies notification timing and silence through executable event plans and source-event replay. To address this challenge, we propose a real-time VLM agent, TEMPI. TEMPI decomposes instructions into atomic event queries and temporal constraints, and uses Scenario Memory to continuously maintain task progress as event evidence arrives, allowing earlier observations to support subsequent decisions beyond the detector's visual window. Even when no notification is required, relevant events continue to update the scenario state. On CoTriggerBench, TEMPI achieves 44.4% instruction-level success, outperforming the strongest closed-source and fine-tuned open-source VLM baselines by 15.6 (Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash-Realtime) and 18.1 (MOSS-VL-Realtime) percentage points, respectively. To support efficient on-device streaming inference, we further optimize the streaming inference pipeline by overlapping partial visual encoding and LLM prefix prefill with frame arrival. On an 8 GB RTX 5060, our optimized detector implementation achieves a 4.90$\times$ speedup.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen, Zekun Qi, Zekai Li
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: ScaleVLA, utilizing a 552B parameter backbone, enhances robot learning efficiency, generalization, and manipulation success compared to smaller Vision-Language-Action models.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: VGGT-VLA-World: Intent-Conditioned 3D World Evolution for Autonomous Driving
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zhaoyang Liu, Zhigui Lin, Kun Jiang, Tianhui Li, Changye Liu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: VGGTWorld-VLA enhances 3D world evolution in autonomous driving by integrating intention-based action conditioning, improving future geometry predictions significantly compared to existing models.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: VGGT provides a strong foundation for geometry-centric world models by recovering unified 3D scene geometry from visual observations. Although recent extensions enable temporal 3D prediction, their future evolution remains weakly conditioned on driving intentions and actions, limiting their ability to model alternative action-dependent futures. We propose \textbf{VGGTWorld-VLA}, an intention-conditioned extension of VGGT-World for controllable 3D world evolution in autonomous driving. First, we introduce an action--semantic conditioning mechanism that injects complementary driving semantics and ego-motion representations into the future-token stream, enabling different future geometry predictions for the same observed scene under alternative ego actions. Second, we develop a geometry--language--action bridge that adapts historical geometry, VLA semantic features, and maneuver and trajectory representations for joint conditioning of future geometry prediction. We evaluate future geometry prediction on NAVSIM, with ablation studies examining the contributions of semantic and action conditioning. Compared with baseline, our method reduces future-depth RMSE by 13.7\% and improves $δ_1$ by 4.11 percentage points on NAVSIM motion subset. Controlled action-input interventions further show that the model uses the supplied action information. These results support semantic and action conditioning for controllable VGGT-based world prediction in autonomous driving.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Visual Cipher Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Reasoning
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Deyao Hong, Jiayi Jiang, Yuchun Chen, Yixuan Shi, Wenyi Li
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: Visual Cipher Bench introduces 40 visual puzzles to evaluate long-horizon visual reasoning in LLM agents, revealing significant challenges in rule discovery from images.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: While language-model agents excel at long-horizon coding and terminal tasks, this success relies on two conditions: explicit text specifications and immediate execution feedback. However, neither condition holds in real-world problems where critical information exists only in images, leaving it unclear whether long-horizon capability transfers from text to visual reasoning. In such visual settings, because rules and clues resist text transcription and lack test-case feedback, agents must repeatedly inspect images, simulate spatial transformations, and autonomously cross-check clues. Despite this challenge, existing evaluations fail to capture such capability: visual reasoning benchmarks largely reduce tasks to single-turn, short-chain question answering, whereas agent benchmarks focus on text-based environments or interactive states that permit trial-and-error. To bridge this gap, we introduce Visual Cipher Bench, a collection of 40 original visual puzzles across four categories: spatial manipulation and simulation, logical constraints and planning, rule induction, and knowledge-based decoding. Each puzzle provides only one to three black-and-white line drawings and a minimal submission instruction, requiring agents to discover the underlying solving mechanism entirely from the images. Across 29 reasoning-effort configurations of eight frontier models, even the strongest model, GPT-6 Astra (max), achieves only 26.7% accuracy, while five of the eight models score below 1%. Yet on a ten-task subset, providing a single non-spoiler mechanism hint boosts accuracy from 12.2% to 51.1%. This sharp contrast shows that the primary bottleneck of current agents lies not in executing multi-step plans, but in autonomously discovering rules from visual evidence. Visual Cipher Bench thus provides a rigorous benchmark for measuring long-horizon visual reasoning in agents.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Haofeng Wang, Xuanyi Liu, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: PhysCapBench is a novel benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, assessing annotation quality across diverse domains to enhance physical AI training and performance.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yuhan Tang, Ke Fan, Xinkai Zou, Baichuan Mo, Kangxin Cui
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper introduces Ask2Decide, a benchmark assessing LLM agents' ability to acquire crucial decision-relevant information from humans, revealing significant challenges in planning accuracy.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: Ego-CEVR is a framework that enhances robot learning by leveraging egocentric videos through distinct global and interaction representation objectives, achieving superior performance and generalization.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Egocentric videos offer a low-cost, scalable source of manipulation experience for robot learning. However, existing methods often fail to tailor their use of egocentric videos and robot demonstrations to the differences in their formats and information content. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns task context through future video prediction, while the interaction module uses this context to interpret wrist observations and learns local execution information through robot action supervision. The distinct learning objectives enable independent pretraining on large-scale human and robot egocentric videos to learn task context, and training on real-robot demonstrations to align the learned representations with fine-grained robot actions. Experiments show leading performance on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, while real-robot evaluations demonstrate generalization across tasks and embodiments.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Non-Imaging Optical Tactile Sensors for Robotics: Transduction Principles, System Integration, and Robotic Applications
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Hao Wu, Yu Feng, Haotian Guo, Huichan Zhao, Changsheng Wu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: This review explores non-imaging optical tactile sensors in robotics, emphasizing their design, integration, and performance in accurately detecting contact variables amidst mechanical influences.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Non-imaging optical tactile sensors encode contact through changes in optical intensity, wavelength, spectra, or photon counts, offering diverse architectures for robotic touch. Their usefulness depends on whether contact variables can be reliably distinguished from coupled mechanical and environmental effects, and whether the resulting information can be delivered in time to guide action. This review develops a unified framework linking mechanical load transmission, optical encoding, readout, and tactile inference to robotic task requirements. It examines reflective and waveguide-based devices, micro/nanofibers, fiber gratings, interferometric and resonant structures, and mechanoluminescent composites. Three considerations emerge across these approaches. First, high optical sensitivity supports accurate tactile estimation only when target variables remain identifiable under the relevant contact and calibration conditions. Second, spatial coverage and feedback timing must be assessed at the system level, accounting for multiplexing, acquisition, demodulation, and inference. Third, device characterization, offline recognition, and closed-loop robotic performance provide distinct levels of evidence and require different evaluation criteria. Representative studies illustrate how these considerations shape force estimation, contact localization, slip correction and distributed interaction. This review concludes with priorities for calibration transfer, reliable interfaces, scalable readout, and task-based validation, providing a basis for selecting and developing non-imaging optical tactile architectures for robotics.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ExtremeDrive: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Critical Driving
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xinhan Li, Yuhong Jiang, Shiyue Zhao, Junzhi Zhang, Chengkun He
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: ExtremeDrive is a comprehensive dataset and benchmark for autonomous driving, focusing on safety-critical scenarios and extreme conditions, enhancing trajectory prediction and driving performance.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Existing autonomous driving datasets and benchmarks provide extensive resources for routine driving, yet real-world data covering safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions remain limited. To address this gap, we present ExtremeDrive, a real-world dataset and benchmark covering emergency maneuvers, complex traffic interactions, and adverse conditions such as slippery or snow-covered roads, alongside routine driving. The dataset comprises 589 driving scenes curated from a larger pool of real-world driving recordings, with calibrated and aligned multisensor data and reviewed annotations of road structure and traffic participants. We further establish a benchmark to evaluate planned trajectories through simulated vehicle execution, measuring safety-related metrics and driving performance. Experiments at equal training set sizes show that incorporating critical driving data reduces trajectory prediction errors and improves mean critical-success rates in critical scenarios. ExtremeDrive provides a unified resource for learning and evaluating autonomous driving in safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: AsymEEF: Bimanual Manipulation with Asymmetric End Effectors
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xiaokang Sun, Ningyue Wang, Kunqi Xu, Guangqi Jiang, Jianglong Ye
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: AsymEEF enables efficient bimanual manipulation by transferring demonstrations across diverse end-effectors, enhancing policy learning and execution success without additional teleoperation.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Teleoperated demonstrations are costly to collect and rarely reusable across end-effectors with different kinematics and action spaces. This burden grows in bimanual manipulation, where each end-effector pair may require new data. We present AsymEEF, a framework for executable cross-end-effector demonstration generation and unified bimanual policy learning. Given a small source dataset, AsymEEF transfers demonstrations to heterogeneous combinations of two-, three-, and five-fingered end-effectors without additional teleoperation. Kinematic teacher anchors provide geometric supervision, while sparse real-world X-Calib anchors correct discrepancies in grasp execution. A shared encoder maps wrist poses and actuator states to a morphology-agnostic latent space, and a morphology-conditioned decoder reconstructs target commands. Generated trajectories undergo replay filtering for task-level executability. The representation also supports a unified bimanual visuomotor policy trained across multiple pairs. Across four simulated and six real-world tasks, AsymEEF improves replay success over adapted transfer baselines, achieves a mean replay-valid expansion gain of 16.6 times in simulation, and is evaluated through downstream policy training on real robots. Project website: https://asymeef.vercel.app/.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ReRead: Wrong Predictions, Useful Representations - Correcting Frozen Robot Policies by Re-reading Their Own Representations
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xu Su, Shunlong Xiao, Qintao Yi, Mingkuan Zhao, Xinmiao Yu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The ReRead method enhances frozen robot policies by correcting action predictions using past representations, improving success rates significantly across various tasks without additional visual encoders.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: When a pretrained robot policy fails on challenging tasks, common remedies include retraining the backbone, adding an external visual encoder, or introducing a memory module. We argue that wrong predictions do not imply wrong representations: a policy can retain the required information yet fail to read it out as the correct action. To test this view, we propose ReRead: with the backbone frozen, a corrector re-reads the current and two previous caches to predict an action residual. The corrector sees no images, is trained solely on offline demonstrations from all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and adds only 4.17% latency. Ablations and interventions show that the correction relies on the backbone's own representations: none of four external visual encoders adds further gain, and swapping in past caches from other trajectories sharply increases action error. On the 11 hardest RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, ReRead improves the success rates of LingBot-VLA, $π_{0.5}$, and Fast-WAM by 23.45, 13.09, and 8.00 percentage points, respectively. In paired evaluation on all 50 tasks, it raises Fast-WAM's average success rate from 90.73% to 92.66%. On a Flexiv dual-arm robot, it raises success on a phase-ambiguous task from 0% to 36%.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ODEWorld: A Continuous Predictive Architecture via Physical-Time Flow
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Dongxiu Liu, Haoyi Niu, Peng Cheng, Yuan Gao, Xirui Kang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: ODEWorld introduces a continuous predictive architecture using Physical-Time Flow and ODEs to enhance efficiency in modeling dynamics, enabling high-quality predictions and planning in robotics.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: In the physical world we inhabit, space and time are fundamentally continuous. However, existing machine learning paradigms for world modeling are largely confined to discrete-time prediction, thereby exhibiting significant inefficiency in capturing the dynamics of physical world. We introduce Physical-Time Flow (PT-Flow), a novel approach that learns a continuous latent velocity field operating in physical time. Crucially, the underlying dynamics of sequential data are parameterized by an ordinary differential equation (ODE) embedded in a well-structured representation space. Under this paradigm, the prediction of future can be recast as temporal integration via an ODE solver in the compressed latent space. Building upon PT-Flow, we construct ODEWorld, a continuous-time latent world model that is both efficient and versatile. By extracting time-variant features and enforcing ODE properties on both the dynamical representation space and the latent velocity field, ODEWorld effectively addresses the long-standing representation collapse issue in latent world model literature. This also enables high-quality image reconstruction even after long-horizon prediction. Moreover, its continuous nature allows for arbitrary temporal resolution and even backward prediction, which is impossible for most discrete-time models. Lastly, ODEWorld can provide rich planning-oriented information to facilitate downstream policy learning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that ODEWorld successfully reconciles planning-conducive dynamics abstraction with visual realism, excelling in both video generation and robotic control. Project page: https://dstate.github.io/odeworld_website/.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: OA-WAM: Object-Addressable World Action Model for Robust Robot Manipulation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yushan Liu, Peibo Sun, Shoujie Li, Yifan Xie, Lingfeng Zhang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: OA-WAM introduces an object-addressable world action model that enhances robot manipulation robustness across varying conditions, achieving superior performance in multiple benchmarks and real-robot tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) learn manipulation by predicting actions and future observations, yet their success drops sharply when the camera viewpoint, object layout or robot initial state changes. Such changes keep the instructed object the same but alter the appearance and pose features the policy observes, which in standard attention also form the keys that locate the object. We introduce OA-WAM, an object-addressable WAM that finds each object by an identity address fixed for the episode and reads its changing state. In every layer of a pretrained multimodal trunk, object-slot keys depend only on the address and frame position, and values carry the current state; the same addresses key the action pointer and index per-object forecasts, which can trigger re-grounding. Fine-tuned on standard LIBERO demonstrations, OA-WAM transfers zero-shot to LIBERO-Plus with 90.5% success, outperforming all ten published baselines. It also leads on LIBERO (99.0%) and, fine-tuned on BridgeData V2, on SimplerEnv WidowX (88.9%). On five real-robot tasks, it succeeds in 89 of 100 nominal trials, versus 73 for the strongest baseline. Ablations trace its robustness to addressing rather than to object slots: with standard attention, slots do no better than a slot-free policy, and addressing them by identity raises geometric success by 10.7 points. Forecasting the addressed objects is likewise a stronger training signal than forecasting image codes.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: EgoEMG: A Multimodal Egocentric Dataset with Bilateral EMG and Vision for Hand Pose Estimation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Ziheng Xi, Jiayi Yu, Yanbo Duan, Yitao Wang, Jinyang Yu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: EgoEMG introduces a multimodal dataset combining bilateral sEMG and egocentric video for improved hand pose estimation, achieving notable accuracy enhancements through feature fusion.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Hand pose estimation from egocentric video is challenging under adverse visual conditions, such as occlusion. Wrist-worn surface electromyography (sEMG) measures muscle activity without requiring visual access to the hand, offering a wearable complement to egocentric cameras. Evaluating their combined use requires synchronized physiological and visual recordings with continuous pose annotations, which existing EMG-based hand pose datasets do not jointly provide. We introduce EgoEMG, a multimodal dataset pairing bilateral wrist sEMG with egocentric video and motion-capture-derived hand poses, supplemented by external multi-view RGB-D recordings. EgoEMG contains 25.9 hours of recordings from 68 participants, covering 60 bare-hand gesture classes and interactions with 10 everyday objects. We establish EMG-only, vision-only, and fusion benchmarks with shared 22-dimensional pose targets and evaluations on unseen users, gestures, and objects. For EMG-only estimation, EMGFormer achieves the lowest overall MAE among the compared methods on EgoEMG and competitive results on EMG2Pose. Our residual fusion model combines ViT and EMGFormer features. Adding EMG reduces error for both single-frame and temporal vision models, with MAE decreasing from $7.39^\circ$ to $7.06^\circ$ for ViT-L. The largest absolute reduction occurs when evaluating interactions with an unseen object. Generalization to unseen users remains challenging. Project page: https://zhenqis123.github.io/egoemg-site/.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Beyond Visual Cues: Semantic-Driven Token Filtering and Expert Routing for Anytime Person ReID
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Jiaxuan Li, Xin Wen, Zhihang Li
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper presents STFER, a framework utilizing Large Vision-Language Models for robust person re-identification across varying conditions by integrating semantic-driven filtering and expert routing.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Any-Time Person Re-identification (AT-ReID) necessitates the robust retrieval of target individuals under arbitrary conditions, encompassing both modality shifts (daytime and nighttime) and extensive clothing-change scenarios, ranging from short-term to long-term intervals. However, existing methods are highly relying on pure visual features, which are prone to change due to environmental and time factors, resulting in significantly performance deterioration under scenarios involving illumination caused modality shifts or cloth-change. In this paper, we propose Semantic-driven Token Filtering and Expert Routing (STFER), a novel framework that leverages the ability of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to generate identity consistency text, which provides identity-discriminative features that are robust to both clothing variations and cross-modality shifts between RGB and IR. Specifically, we employ instructions to guide the LVLM in generating identity-intrinsic semantic text that captures biometric constants for the semantic model driven. The text token is further used for Semantic-driven Visual Token Filtering (SVTF), which enhances informative visual regions and suppresses redundant background noise. Meanwhile, the text token is also used for Semantic-driven Expert Routing (SER), which integrates the semantic text into expert routing, resulting in more robust multi-scenario gating. Extensive experiments on the Any-Time ReID dataset (AT-USTC) demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art results. Moreover, the model trained on AT-USTC was evaluated across 5 widely-used ReID benchmarks demonstrating superior generalization capabilities with highly competitive results. Our code will be available soon.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: PlanDiv: Test-Time Scaling with Latent Plans for Vision-Language-Action Models
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Hanbo Zhang, Lianlei Shan, Liuhaichen Yang, Zezhi Tang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: PlanDiv enhances vision-language-action models by generating diverse action candidates through latent plans, significantly improving task success rates compared to traditional resampling methods.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Test-time scaling improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies by drawing several action candidates and executing the best one. We find that its returns diminish quickly when the candidates are resampled from one decoder: they differ by noise rather than by plan, and for each of three resampling sources, going from four to eight candidates adds only 0.06-0.07 to the average number of completed tasks on CALVIN. We introduce PlanDiv, an action head that makes the candidates differ by plan: a lightweight planner proposes K latent plan hypotheses, a shared masked-diffusion executor decodes one action chunk per plan from a single backbone pass, and the policy executes the chunk that its own likelihood ranks highest. The plans are learned from demonstrations alone, without plan labels or rewards. With the backbone, data and training recipe held fixed, eight plan-conditioned candidates raise five-task chain success on CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D from 56.9% to 69.9%, while eight candidates from autoregressive, plan-free or same-plan resampling reach at most 64.9%. The same-plan baseline is PlanDiv's own checkpoint with the plan held fixed, so this gap comes from the plans, not from drawing more samples. On LIBERO-Long, four plans remove 40% of single-candidate failures, against at most 21% for matched resampling. On a real Franka arm the gain appears where a task admits more than one solution: PlanDiv is on par with a single-output OpenVLA-OFT+ baseline on a one-solution task and succeeds in 51 of 54 trials against 40 of 54 on two tasks with two solutions.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Beyond Vehicle-Centric Data: Scaling Autonomous Driving through Roadside-to-Vehicle Generation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yichen Zhang, Zihan Wang, Hao Chen, Runyi Huang, Ruixue Zong
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The AnyR2V framework transforms roadside traffic data into diverse vehicle-centric training videos, enhancing autonomous driving model performance by generating multi-perspective datasets.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Training autonomous driving models requires large and diverse datasets, collected primarily by vehicles. Scaling them entails investment in fleet operation, data processing and annotation. Road infrastructure records traffic and multi-vehicle interactions, yet the viewpoint gap between roadside and onboard sensors limits its direct use for training. Here we introduce AnyR2V, a framework that transforms multimodal roadside observations into seven-camera surround-view videos for different vehicle perspectives. It aggregates sequential observations into a shared scene representation of geometry and road-user motion, then renders appearance, depth and layout conditions along target-vehicle trajectories. Supervised by spatiotemporally aligned roadside-vehicle pairs, AnyR2V generates surround-view videos guided by scene structure and road-user motion. Existing roadside 3D bounding boxes are transformed into target-vehicle coordinates and paired with generated images, allowing one traffic recording and its annotations to yield training data from multiple vehicle perspectives. We construct R2V360, a dataset of 89 real traffic sequences at an urban intersection, with aligned multimodal roadside data and onboard surround-view videos. AnyR2V outperforms six scene reconstruction methods in image fidelity and in depth and semantic agreement between generated and real onboard images. We further evaluate generated videos along other vehicles' trajectories by adding them to real training data. Adding generated frames equal to 50% of the original real training frame count improves mean average precision (mAP) by 3.3-3.4 AP-points across three 3D object detectors on the real onboard test set, relative to real-data-only baselines. These results demonstrate that roadside traffic records can provide training data from multiple vehicle perspectives, offering a new data source for autonomous driving.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: M-CROSS: A Multisensor Simulation Dataset for SLAM across Water--Land Transitions
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yan Dong, Tianyi Wu, Junyu Yang, Shaoqiang Qiu, Zefeng Yan
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: M-CROSS is a novel multisensor simulation dataset for SLAM, addressing localization challenges in water-land transitions with new metrics and demonstrating existing methods' inadequacies.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Water--land cross-domain robots require continuous localization across land, transition and underwater phases, where sensor characteristics and availability change abruptly. Existing datasets and conventional metrics are not designed to capture transition-induced degradation and failures. We present \textbf{M-CROSS}, to the best of our knowledge, the first multisensor simulation dataset and benchmark for SLAM across continuous water--land transitions. It provides synchronized LiDAR, sonar, stereo camera, IMU, DVL, and depth measurements; 6DoF pose ground truth; sensor-wise medium-state annotations; and medium-dependent sensor degradation models. We establish a transition-aware protocol comprising the Trajectory Completion Rate (TCR), Piecewise Absolute Pose Error (PW-APE), Transition End Error (TEE), and Transition Survival Period (TSP), which measure trajectory completion, single-domain accuracy, transition-induced error, and localization survival under prolonged partial immersion, respectively. Experiments with 6 representative SLAM systems show that existing methods fail to maintain both localization accuracy and trajectory continuity across the full set of water--land transitions, exhibiting transition-induced drift, trajectory discontinuities, and tracking failures. M-CROSS is publicly available https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MCross-Dataset

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Kuan Zhang, Zirong Chen
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: RISE-RL enhances open-ended reinforcement learning by selectively exploring trajectories based on missed rubric criteria, significantly improving performance across various benchmarks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) for open-ended tasks is challenging because responses must satisfy multidimensional criteria without following a single correct generation trajectory. Existing rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) methods compress fine-grained criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards, making persistent capability gaps difficult to target under limited on-policy exploration. We propose $\textbf{RISE-RL}$ (Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration), which uses repeatedly missed rubric criteria to elicit privileged trajectories that are difficult to discover through unguided exploration alone. RISE-RL retains only trajectories whose complete-rubric reward exceeds the mean reward of natural rollouts, and then re-evaluates them under the original prompt to emphasize behaviors that remain weakly supported by the natural policy. The resulting guidance signal is optimized through a separate auxiliary objective and removed once its additional benefit diminishes. Experiments with 4B and 14B models across writing, chat, health, and science show that RISE-RL achieves the highest mean score on every evaluated benchmark under guidance-free evaluation. Compared with standard Rubric-RL, it improves the average score by 1.3 points at the 4B scale and $\textbf{3.3 points at the 14B scale}$, including a $\textbf{6.0-point}$ gain on CreativeWriting-V3. It also improves creative-writing diversity and yields gains on objectively scored medical and scientific benchmarks. These results indicate that selective internalization through reward filtering and policy support shaping is effective for open-ended reinforcement learning.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: LatentUM: Unleashing the Potential of Interleaved Cross-Modal Reasoning via a Latent-Space Unified Model
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Jiachun Jin, Zetong Zhou, Xiao Yang, Hao Zhang, Pengfei Liu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: LatentUM introduces a unified model that enhances interleaved cross-modal reasoning by utilizing a shared semantic latent space, achieving state-of-the-art performance in visual tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Unified models (UMs) hold promise for their ability to understand and generate content across heterogeneous modalities. Compared to merely generating visual content, the use of UMs for interleaved cross-modal reasoning is more promising and valuable, e.g., for solving understanding problems that require dense visual thinking, improving visual generation through self-reflection, or modeling visual dynamics of the physical world guided by stepwise action interventions. However, existing UMs typically rely on pixel decoding as a bridge when their visual representations for understanding and generation are disjoint, which is both ineffective and computationally cumbersome.
