On the learning side, \user adopts a fully asynchronous training framework, designs a persistent and cache-aware replay buffer, and provides extensible abstractions for rewards, algorithms, and policies. Experiments in both simulation and the real world demonstrate that \user supports multi-robot coordination, heterogeneous manipulators, cloud-edge training with large models, and long-running asynchronous training. Together, these capabilities establish \user as a unified and extensible systems foundation for online real-world policy learning.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: ReST-RL: Reinforcing LLM Reasoning through Unified Self-Training and Value-Guided Search
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Sining Zhoubian, Dan Zhang, Jie Tang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: ReST-RL enhances LLM reasoning accuracy through a unified self-training and value-guided search framework, outperforming existing reinforcement learning and decoding methods across various benchmarks.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: With respect to improving the reasoning accuracy of LLMs, the representative reinforcement learning (RL) method - Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) - has achieved critical success, yet it still suffers from the issue of insignificant reward signals. This paper introduces ReST-RL, a unified Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) policy-value framework that reconnects policy optimization and value-guided search to improve LLM reasoning ability. Firstly, ReST-GRPO adopts an optimized ReST-style algorithm to reshape the policy-induced trajectory distribution by increasing the reward variance of GRPO sampling and exposing the policy to more informative partial states, thereby improving training efficiency and effectiveness. Then, we further introduce a decoding optimization method, VM-MCTS, which trains a Value Model (VM) from self-collected Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) targets and deploys it through an adapted MCTS algorithm to provide precise process signals and verification scores, further enhancing reasoning accuracy. These two stages are internally dependent - ReST-GRPO yields higher quality trajectories for value learning with VM-MCTS, which in turn enables more effective inference-time search. We validate our framework on multiple coding benchmarks (e.g., APPS, BigCodeBench, and HumanEval), where it significantly outperforms other reinforcement training baselines (naive GRPO, DAPO, and ReST-DPO), as well as decoding and verification baselines (e.g., PRM-BoN and ORM-MCTS), indicating its power to strengthen LLM reasoning capability. Moreover, we further evaluate ReST-RL on out-of-domain math and science reasoning tasks, where it achieves improved performance without target-domain tuning and favorable end-to-end efficiency trade-offs, providing preliminary transfer evidence beyond our primary coding domain.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: SARGO: Agreement-Gated Reinforcement and Suppression via On-Policy Self-Guidance for Visual Hallucination Mitigation
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Jinyu Li, Zhiming Zhang, Hao Fang, Hongyao Yu, Bin Chen
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: SARGO introduces a post-training framework that selectively reinforces accurate visual information while mitigating hallucinations in vision-language models through on-policy self-guidance.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language models remain susceptible to visual hallucinations, often mixing grounded information with unsupported claims in the same response. Response-level reinforcement learning assigns a shared advantage to all tokens in a response, causing negative updates to suppress correct information alongside unsupported claims. To reduce hallucination while preserving useful visual information, we introduce SARGO (Self-guided Advantage-Routed Grounding Optimization), a post-training framework for selective reinforcement and suppression through on-policy self-guidance. Direct and reciprocal weighting gives better-supported tokens stronger reinforcement on positive updates and weaker penalties on negative updates. Agreement between overall and hallucination-specific advantages selects when to apply this guidance. At the response level, a reference-calibrated reward couples factuality with the retention and expansion of grounded information, discouraging lower hallucination scores obtained through omission. Experiments on Qwen3-VL-4B, Qwen3-VL-8B, and Gemma3-4B demonstrate that SARGO outperforms the evaluated mitigation baselines across Obj-Hal, AMBER, THRONE, and SHR evaluations. SARGO achieves these gains while preserving useful visual information and general multimodal capabilities.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Yuan Wei, Ying Wei
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper explores how on-policy distillation reshapes interaction patterns in language-model agents across various domains, revealing both improvements and negative transfers in performance.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Guangzhi Sun, Zhonghao Zhai, Yixuan Li, Chao Zhang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The VEX framework enhances computer-use agents by leveraging audio-visual understanding from tutorial videos for improved task execution and self-verification, achieving significant performance gains.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior. Following a watch-act-rewatch paradigm, the agent extracts procedural guidance from tutorial videos containing visual demonstrations and spoken explanations, executes tasks, and verifies its progress by rewatching its execution as video. We instantiate VEX with video-SALMONN-VEX, a 9B-scale audio-visual computer-use agent built on the video-SALMONN 2 architecture with a Qwen3.5-9B backbone. We further introduce Action-Grounded Guide Optimization (AGGO), a reinforcement learning method that optimizes video-derived guidance for downstream action prediction, and augment AgentNet, OSWorld, and CUA-Gym with over 24K real-world tutorial videos. Experiments on OSWorld and a complementary subset of CUA-Gym demonstrate consistent improvements, with video-SALMONN-VEX achieving a 22% relative increase in task success over its Qwen3.5 backbone on OSWorld. Moreover, its generated guidance improves Gemini-3.5-flash by 10% relatively on OSWorld. These results highlight the potential of audio-visual understanding as a unified interface for procedural learning and self-verification in computer-use agents.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Recognizing Events Is Not Enough: Why Streaming VLMs Struggle in Compositional Instruction Triggering
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Yehua Huang, Penglei Sun, Xiang Li, Jinhao Zhou, Jiawen Wen
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper introduces TEMPI, a real-time VLM agent that improves compositional instruction execution in streaming video by effectively managing temporal constraints and task progress.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Recognizing individual events does not guarantee correct execution of compositional instructions in streaming video. For example, given the request "Notify me when the pot boils after someone turns on the stove and leaves the kitchen", existing models may recognize the individual events yet notify too early or miss the intended moment, failing to track how their temporal conditions are satisfied over time. To evaluate this gap, we introduce CoTriggerBench, which composes annotated video events into temporally constrained instructions and verifies notification timing and silence through executable event plans and source-event replay. To address this challenge, we propose a real-time VLM agent, TEMPI. TEMPI decomposes instructions into atomic event queries and temporal constraints, and uses Scenario Memory to continuously maintain task progress as event evidence arrives, allowing earlier observations to support subsequent decisions beyond the detector's visual window. Even when no notification is required, relevant events continue to update the scenario state. On CoTriggerBench, TEMPI achieves 44.4% instruction-level success, outperforming the strongest closed-source and fine-tuned open-source VLM baselines by 15.6 (Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash-Realtime) and 18.1 (MOSS-VL-Realtime) percentage points, respectively. To support efficient on-device streaming inference, we further optimize the streaming inference pipeline by overlapping partial visual encoding and LLM prefix prefill with frame arrival. On an 8 GB RTX 5060, our optimized detector implementation achieves a 4.90$\times$ speedup.

Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).title: UnderOneFacade: Worldwide Facade Semantic Segmentation Benchmark Dataset
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).authors_text: Yi Wang, Fan Wang, Prabin Gyawali, Ziyang Xu, Anna Klimkowska
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).summary: UnderOneFacade introduces a comprehensive 3D facade segmentation benchmark with 2.7 billion annotated points, addressing cross-domain generalization challenges in architectural recognition.
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).debug_abstract: Globally consistent semantic digital twins require centimeter-accurate and geographically transferable 3D facade segmentation. However, progress in facade parsing is limited by the lack of large-scale, standardized benchmarks for evaluating cross-domain generalization. Existing datasets are geographically narrow, semantically inconsistent, or insufficiently precise. We introduce UnderOneFacade, the largest cross-country and cross-continent 3D facade benchmark to date, comprising centimeter-accurate point clouds with hierarchical, harmonized, and architecturally grounded semantic labels totaling 2.7 billion annotated points. Through a systematic evaluation of representative point-, graph- and transformer-based architectures, we show that current methods struggle to recognize fine-grained architectural elements and degrade significantly across geographic domains, with the best models achieving only up to 33 IoU on the fine-grained LoFG3 benchmark. By combining geometric precision with standardized semantics at unprecedented scale, UnderOneFacade establishes a rigorous benchmark for developing robust and transferable 3D segmentation models. The dataset, evaluation scripts, and pretrained models will be released upon publication.

Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).title: MemReg: Streaming Outdoor LiDAR Point Cloud Registration with Hybrid Memory Buffers
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).authors_text: Jiuming Liu, Mengmeng Liu, Guangming Wang, Lihao Liu, Michael Ying Yang
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).summary: MemReg introduces a multi-frame outdoor LiDAR registration network utilizing hybrid memory buffers to enhance performance by leveraging temporal correlations in streaming sequences.
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).debug_abstract: Prior outdoor LiDAR registration works are commonly limited by the pair-wise input paradigm, which neglects temporal correlations inherent within streaming sequences. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-frame outdoor point cloud registration network for streaming LiDAR scans enhanced with pose-related memory buffers. The key observation is that long-term temporal LiDAR sequences can provide rich global contextual information to complete sparse measurements, filter outliers, and address low-overlap problems, thereby boosting registration performance. Specifically, two hybrid memory buffers are designed, including an implicit memory feature buffer and an explicit memory pose buffer, to store and dynamically update pose-related temporal features. Moreover, a novel dynamic history weighting module is developed to adaptively fuse current and history pose-related features. Extensive experiments on three outdoor datasets, including KITTI, nuScenes, and Apollo-Southbay, demonstrate state-of-the-art performance of MemReg, surpassing all previous pair-wise methods and also multi-frame SLAM systems. Our method also generalizes surprisingly well to multiview indoor registration scenarios with rather competitive performance on 3DMatch, 3DLoMatch, and ScanNet. Code will be released at https://github.com/IRMVLab/MemReg.

Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).title: UNIVERSE: Unified Video Action Models for Autonomous Driving with Flexible Mask-Modulated Modality Generation
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).authors_text: Mengmeng Liu, Diankun Zhang, Jiuming Liu, Jianfeng Cui, Hongwei Xie
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).summary: UNIVERSE introduces a unified video-action model using a mask-modulated Diffusion Transformer for efficient autonomous driving, enhancing action generalization and enabling flexible inference without costly future-video generation.
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) can improve action generalization in autonomous driving by learning scene dynamics through dense future-video supervision. However, deploying such models often requires costly future-video generation, while architectures that bypass video rollout typically separate video and action parameters or alter their learned dependencies at inference. We introduce UNIVERSE, a unified video-action model built on a single mask-modulated Diffusion Transformer (DiT) that combines shared-parameter learning with modality-independent inference. Its Modality-Decoupling Visibility Mask allows future video and trajectory tokens to attend to a common historical context while blocking mutual attention between the two future modalities. As a result, future-video supervision directly updates the parameters used for trajectory denoising, yet video tokens can be omitted at test time without changing the trajectory branch's training-time attention dependencies. The same model supports trajectory-only, video-only, and joint video-action generation. Trajectory-only inference achieves a 4.3x speedup over coupled video-action rollout with comparable planning accuracy. UNIVERSE achieves 91.0 PDMS on NAVSIM, compared with 89.6 for a Two-DiT variant, and demonstrates strong zero-shot transfer to nuScenes and Bench2Drive without target-domain fine-tuning. Controlled ablations further support the complementary benefits of shared parameters, dense video co-training, and modality-decoupled visibility.

Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).title: Stable Transformer-Actor-Critic Model Predictive Control: A Contraction Analysis Approach
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).authors_text: Antonio Marino, Valerio Modugno, Marco Cognetti
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).summary: This paper presents a robust Transformer-Actor-Critic MPC framework ensuring physical safety and stability through mathematical constraints and novel contraction analysis for complex control tasks.
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).debug_abstract: Hybrid optimization-learning frameworks, such as Actor-Critic Model Predictive Control (MPC), rely on dynamically adjusting cost parameters to manage complex control landscapes. In this paper, we introduce a certifiably robust Transformer-Actor-Critic MPC architecture that leverages history-aware sequence models to shape local optimization while maintaining strict physical safety guarantees. First, we mathematically constrain the Transformer sequence models to satisfy global incremental Input-to-State Stability ($δ$ISS). Second, we integrate these neural Lipschitz bounds with Riemannian contraction theory, deriving a novel coupled small-gain condition that enforces uniform closed-loop contraction stability across the interconnected system. Evaluated on quadrotor control and decentralized multi-agent navigation tasks subjected to severe observation noise and process disturbances, our closed-loop stable formulation successfully translates theoretical bounds into physical safety.

Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.authors_text: Guangzhi Sun, Zhonghao Zhai, Yixuan Li, Chao Zhang
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.summary: The VEX framework enhances computer-use agents by leveraging audio-visual understanding from tutorial videos for improved task execution and self-verification, achieving significant performance gains.
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior. Following a watch-act-rewatch paradigm, the agent extracts procedural guidance from tutorial videos containing visual demonstrations and spoken explanations, executes tasks, and verifies its progress by rewatching its execution as video. We instantiate VEX with video-SALMONN-VEX, a 9B-scale audio-visual computer-use agent built on the video-SALMONN 2 architecture with a Qwen3.5-9B backbone. We further introduce Action-Grounded Guide Optimization (AGGO), a reinforcement learning method that optimizes video-derived guidance for downstream action prediction, and augment AgentNet, OSWorld, and CUA-Gym with over 24K real-world tutorial videos. Experiments on OSWorld and a complementary subset of CUA-Gym demonstrate consistent improvements, with video-SALMONN-VEX achieving a 22% relative increase in task success over its Qwen3.5 backbone on OSWorld. Moreover, its generated guidance improves Gemini-3.5-flash by 10% relatively on OSWorld. These results highlight the potential of audio-visual understanding as a unified interface for procedural learning and self-verification in computer-use agents.

厦门大学.title: SIRI: Self-Internalizing Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Skills for LLM Agent Training
厦门大学.authors_text: Zhongyu He, Yuanfan Li, Fei Huang, Tianyu Chen, Siyuan Chen
厦门大学.summary: SIRI introduces a self-internalizing framework for LLM agents to autonomously discover and validate skills, enhancing performance without external generators or inference-time dependencies.
厦门大学.debug_abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can benefit from reusable skills, yet existing skill-based methods often rely on external skill generators during training or persistent skill retrieval at inference, increasing engineering complexity, context length, and deployment latency. We propose Self-Internalizing Reinforcement learning with Intrinsic skills (SIRI), a three-phase framework that enables agents to discover, validate, and internalize skills without external skill generators or inference-time skill banks. SIRI first warms up the policy with GiGPO to acquire basic interaction ability and collect successful skill-free trajectories. It then performs self-skill mining, where the current policy summarizes compact skills from its own successful plain rollouts and validates them through paired skill-augmented and skill-free rollouts. Finally, SIRI distills only beneficial skill-guided action tokens into the plain policy using trajectory-level utility and action-level advantage. At inference, the agent runs with the original prompt only. On ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, SIRI improves GiGPO from 0.908 to 0.930 on ALFWorld and from 0.728 to 0.813 on WebShop, outperforming prompt-based, RL-based, and memory-augmented baselines. Further analysis shows that our self-mining strategy can achieve performance comparable to distillation with closed-source large model.

厦门大学.title: Feature-Space Latent Forecasting for Endoscopic Surgical Video Understanding
厦门大学.summary: The paper presents a feature-space semantic forecasting framework for endoscopic video understanding, enhancing surgical workflow prediction by modeling temporal dynamics in latent representations.
厦门大学.debug_abstract: Surgical workflow assistance is inherently anticipatory: systems must reason about how procedures evolve, not just recognize the current frame. However, many prior approaches perform prediction in pixel space by synthesizing future frames, which primarily focuses on appearance fidelity rather than the semantic representations required for downstream reasoning. To address this limitation, we propose a feature-space semantic forecasting framework that models temporal dynamics directly within the representations of a frozen Vision Foundation Model (VFM). Specifically, we build a hierarchical target representation from multi-layer VFM features, replace future-frame feature tokens with learnable \texttt{[MASK]} tokens, and train a masked transformer to forecast the corresponding future latent features from observed context, thereby formulating procedural evolution as masked future feature prediction. Experiments on public laparoscopic benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements in phase anticipation, multi-label tool presence prediction, and remaining-time estimation over RGB-based forecasting baselines, while enabling a plug-and-play representation interface for lightweight downstream heads.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen, Zekun Qi, Zekai Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: ScaleVLA, utilizing a 552B parameter backbone, enhances robot learning efficiency, generalization, and manipulation success compared to smaller Vision-Language-Action models.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Hanlin Tian, Sihan Zhu, Zhao Yang, Yuxiang Wang, Zhiquan Hu
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: DetourBench introduces a trajectory-level evaluation framework for interactive agents, emphasizing minimum-action bounds to distinguish between efficient and inefficient decision-making processes.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists. We present DetourBench, which constrains the environment until that minimum is computable. Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery. Exhaustive search yields the full-information minimum action count $L_0$ with a replayable witness; from graph-recoverable terminal states it also yields exact residual work $R_T$, which separates an episode that stopped one access short from one that wandered, while an irreversible wrong commitment is recorded as having no finite residual distance rather than assigned one. Success, attainment, residual progress, and normalized detour are reported separately. Across 375 scored episodes --- five model endpoints, 25 integrated tasks, three repeats --- success ranges from 58.7% to 96.0% while conditional attainment ranges from 0.803 to 0.890 and orders the models differently. Among recoverable failures, residual work separates near-complete trajectories from costly incompletion and from irreversible commitment. We open-source the instances, oracle witnesses, and evaluation harness at https://github.com/DatagridsAI/DetourBench.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Fengmin Wu, Sicong Liu, Zimu Zhou, Chenren Xu, Wanbing Zhao
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: UbiHearo is a mobile assistant for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing users that provides scenario-aware sound guidance through a neuro-symbolic approach, enhancing situational awareness and personalized responses.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. However, existing mobile assistants largely reduce acoustic scenes to isolated labels or generic alerts, failing to provide contextual guidance when the same sound implies different risks across scenarios. We present \sysname, a mobile hearing assistant agent that closes the sensing--reasoning--action loop for \textit{scenario-aware} and \textit{personalized} DHH assistance. \sysname adopts a \textit{neuro-symbolic} design that transforms continuous acoustic and physical context streams into structured intermediate representations (IRs) for controllable reasoning and guidance. It introduces three key mechanisms. \textit{First}, a perception-thresholded sensing mechanism enables energy-efficient always-on awareness by activating processing only for perceptually meaningful events while preserving safety-critical cues through deterministic overrides. \textit{Second}, a staged neuro-symbolic reasoning framework performs promptless scenario understanding by conditioning an on-device audio-language model on structured IRs instead of user-authored context descriptions. \textit{Third}, a bounded human-in-the-loop personalization mechanism adapts user-specific guidance through lightweight on-device decision-boundary updates while preserving population-aligned reasoning. We evaluate \sysname on smartphones and in-vehicle systems across diverse scenarios. It achieves favorable accuracy--latency--energy tradeoffs and personalized guidance.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haofeng Wang, Xuanyi Liu, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: PhysCapBench is a novel benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, assessing annotation quality across diverse domains to enhance physical AI training and performance.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yuhan Tang, Ke Fan, Xinkai Zou, Baichuan Mo, Kangxin Cui
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper introduces Ask2Decide, a benchmark assessing LLM agents' ability to acquire crucial decision-relevant information from humans, revealing significant challenges in planning accuracy.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: An LLM-assisted theoretical model for aeroengine installation noise scattering
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper presents a theoretical model for aeroengine noise scattering using LLM-assisted algebraic manipulation, demonstrating AI's potential in theoretical fluid mechanics research.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: A theoretical model is developed for the canonical problem of aeroengine fan noise impinging on, and scattering from, a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate. The model chains two Wiener--Hopf problems in different coordinate systems. The first stage solves the duct-radiation problem analytically in axisymmetric cylindrical coordinates. The second stage expands the field incident on the plate into a double angular spectrum of plane waves: the axial spectrum is inherited from the first stage, while the spanwise spectrum is generated by a Weyl--Sommerfeld expansion of the cylindrical harmonics. Each spectral component is then scattered by the plate. The mathematical crux is the coordinate transformation between the axisymmetric duct frame and the Cartesian plate frame. The core physical insight--that the Weyl--Sommerfeld identity provides an exact spectral bridge between these systems--originates entirely with the authors. The heavy algebra of translating between the two spectral representations, together with the associated numerical verification, was carried out with the assistance of a large language model (LLM), under strict human oversight and independent numerical cross-checking. This division of labour enables the LLM to handle tedious symbolic manipulation without compromising rigour. Results are presented for spinning modes radiating from a cylindrical duct with a subsonic jet into a quiescent ambient. The case study demonstrates that, under systematic verification, LLMs can accelerate tedious algebra in theoretical fluid mechanics, contributing a concrete empirical example to the broader discussion on AI's role in theoretical research.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Learning and Verifying Progress: Closed-Loop Agentic Planning with Progress-Enhanced Execution for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Navigation
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Kangjie Zhou, Sukai Wang, Yuhan Xiao, Qinghang Liu, Zhejia Wen
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: LeaP-VLN enhances long-horizon vision-language navigation by integrating progress-aware execution and verification, improving agent recovery from errors and achieving state-of-the-art success rates.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Long-horizon vision-language navigation (VLN) requires agents to track instruction progress and recover from local errors before they propagate across subtasks. However, executors trained on expert trajectories encounter policy-induced state shifts during deployment, and their stop signals do not reliably indicate subtask completion. We introduce Learning and Verifying Progress for VLN (LeaP-VLN), an agentic VLN system that couples progress-aware execution with independent progress verification through plan--execute--verify--recover cycles. LeaP-VLN leverages progress both explicitly, through a progress verifier that verifies subtask completion before the agent advances and triggers dual-phase recovery upon route deviation, and implicitly, by co-training the executor on progress reasoning and action prediction to enhance the executor's progress awareness and corrective control. To adapt the executor to this closed-loop interface, we propose a two-stage progress-enhanced curriculum: behavior cloning on expert demonstrations, followed by joint training on demonstrations, expert action corrections, and progress-reasoning supervision. Policy-generated trajectories expose the executor to both intra-subtask drift and inter-subtask state shifts, aligning training with the deviations encountered during closed-loop execution. Extensive experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE demonstrate state-of-the-art success rates among monocular methods trained without additional navigation datasets, while real-world experiments further validate the effectiveness of LeaP-VLN in long-horizon navigation.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Glance, then Select: Evidence-Tempered Visual Token Selection for Extremely Compressed Multimodal LLMs
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yuxuan Wang, Guangxiang Zhao, Yuxuan Tian, Yahui Han, Xinyu Tan
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The Glance-ETD framework efficiently reduces visual tokens in multimodal large language models, maintaining high performance while significantly speeding up processing and improving token selection.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) encode a high-resolution image into thousands of visual tokens, which dominate the cost of the prefill stage. Visual token reduction removes most of these tokens, but two problems remain at extreme budgets. The vision encoder still processes every patch of the image, and the few surviving tokens often miss the small regions that hold the answer. In this paper, we propose Glance-ETD, a two-stage token reduction framework guided by a lightweight question-conditioned scorer. In the first stage, a glance encoder views the image at low resolution and re-encodes only the question-relevant regions at native resolution. In the second stage, Evidence-Tempered Diversity (ETD) selects the final tokens by combining diversity with the evidence predicted by the scorer, so that the kept tokens cover the scene and retain the answer. A single-rollout self-distillation recipe trains the MLLM with the glance encoder. With only 5% of the visual tokens, Glance-ETD retains 91.6% of the full-token performance of Qwen3.5-4B across fourteen benchmarks and outperforms the strongest prior method, LT-OPD, by 17.3 points and the same training recipe with DivPrune by 6.0. It also speeds up the time to first token on 4K images by 3.1x and generalizes to three other MLLMs and to high-resolution document benchmarks, with the largest gains on text-rich tasks.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Jiajun Sun, Zeyu Zhang, Zeyu Ren, Guangfeng Jiang, Yang Zhao
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: PanDWM introduces a panoramic 4D driving world model that enhances video generation efficiency and consistency by integrating multiple camera views into a continuous 360° image.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one $360^\circ$ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched $360^\circ$ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at $8$-$46\times$ their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Jiarui Dong, Zhiheng Liang, Yanjun Li, Zeyu Zhang, Heejeong Nam
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: JEPA4R enhances JEPA world models by enabling 4D point planning from depth-camera point clouds, achieving superior performance in robotic manipulation tasks and zero-shot real-world application.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Kuan Zhang, Zirong Chen
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: RISE-RL enhances open-ended reinforcement learning by selectively exploring trajectories based on missed rubric criteria, significantly improving performance across various benchmarks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) for open-ended tasks is challenging because responses must satisfy multidimensional criteria without following a single correct generation trajectory. Existing rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) methods compress fine-grained criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards, making persistent capability gaps difficult to target under limited on-policy exploration. We propose $\textbf{RISE-RL}$ (Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration), which uses repeatedly missed rubric criteria to elicit privileged trajectories that are difficult to discover through unguided exploration alone. RISE-RL retains only trajectories whose complete-rubric reward exceeds the mean reward of natural rollouts, and then re-evaluates them under the original prompt to emphasize behaviors that remain weakly supported by the natural policy. The resulting guidance signal is optimized through a separate auxiliary objective and removed once its additional benefit diminishes. Experiments with 4B and 14B models across writing, chat, health, and science show that RISE-RL achieves the highest mean score on every evaluated benchmark under guidance-free evaluation. Compared with standard Rubric-RL, it improves the average score by 1.3 points at the 4B scale and $\textbf{3.3 points at the 14B scale}$, including a $\textbf{6.0-point}$ gain on CreativeWriting-V3. It also improves creative-writing diversity and yields gains on objectively scored medical and scientific benchmarks. These results indicate that selective internalization through reward filtering and policy support shaping is effective for open-ended reinforcement learning.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: TARGO and TARGO-Net: Benchmarking Target-driven Object Grasping under Occlusions
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yan Xia, Ran Ding, Ziyuan Qin, Guanqi Zhan, Kaichen Zhou
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper introduces TARGO, a benchmark dataset for target-driven grasping under occlusions, and TARGO-Net, a robust model that improves grasp prediction accuracy in cluttered environments.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Predicting 6-DoF grasp poses from a single RGB-D frame has recently achieved impressive accuracy, yet performance can degrade significantly when the target object is heavily occluded by clutter. In this paper, we establish TARGO, the first benchmark dataset for TARget-driven Grasping under Occlusions, and introduce TARGO-Net, a grasp prediction model designed for visual occlusion. Our main contributions are fourfold: 1) We identify the visual occlusion challenge in single-view RGB-D 6-DoF grasping and show that current state-of-the-art models still suffer under severe occlusion. 2) We propose the TARGO dataset, which supports training and testing 6-DoF grasp models across different visual occlusion levels and enables robustness evaluation in real-world scenarios. 3) We devise TARGO-Net, a transformer-based grasping model with a target completion module and target-scene cross-attention, which achieves the most robust performance across all visual occlusion levels. 4) We show that target completion, number of occluders, and target minimum dimension also relate to grasp success in addition to visual occlusion.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Yuan Wei, Ying Wei
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper explores how on-policy distillation reshapes interaction patterns in language-model agents across various domains, revealing both improvements and negative transfers in performance.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Passage-Focused Soft Coordination for Hierarchical Multi-Robot Navigation in Bottleneck Environments
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Haoze Dong, Stepan Dergachev, Meng Guo, Konstantin Yakovlev, Zhongkui Li
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The proposed passage-focused framework enhances multi-robot navigation by integrating soft global coordination with flexible local execution, achieving high success rates and efficient collision avoidance.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: In multi-robot navigation, rigid global schedules are sensitive to execution deviations, while local methods lack long-horizon coordination. We propose a passage-focused framework combining soft global coordination with flexible local execution. A passage-induced graph of convex sets supports priority-ordered planning with two levels of soft coordination. Passage-aware route selection accounts for passage usage and traversal directions, while route-restricted continuous space-time planning penalizes temporal conflicts. The resulting references guide a model predictive path integral controller that avoids collisions online. Adaptive temporal and geometric tracking accommodates execution deviations, while selective replanning maintains coordination without rigid trajectory reservations. Across 1,200 instances in 4 different environments with 5-30 robots, the framework achieves a near-perfect success rate and outperforms evaluated baselines in makespan and flowtime. Hardware experiments with 8 robots demonstrate successful completion of all trials without collisions. These results highlight the effectiveness of passage-focused coordination in balancing long-horizon cooperation with flexible execution.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen, Zekun Qi, Zekai Li
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: ScaleVLA, utilizing a 552B parameter backbone, enhances robot learning efficiency, generalization, and manipulation success compared to smaller Vision-Language-Action models.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. 具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. 具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: An LLM-assisted theoretical model for aeroengine installation noise scattering
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper presents a theoretical model for aeroengine noise scattering using LLM-assisted algebraic manipulation, demonstrating AI's potential in theoretical fluid mechanics research.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: A theoretical model is developed for the canonical problem of aeroengine fan noise impinging on, and scattering from, a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate. The second stage expands the field incident on the plate into a double angular spectrum of plane waves: the axial spectrum is inherited from the first stage, while the spanwise spectrum is generated by a Weyl--Sommerfeld expansion of the cylindrical harmonics. Each spectral component is then scattered by the plate. The mathematical crux is the coordinate transformation between the axisymmetric duct frame and the Cartesian plate frame. The core physical insight--that the Weyl--Sommerfeld identity provides an exact spectral bridge between these systems--originates entirely with the authors. The heavy algebra of translating between the two spectral representations, together with the associated numerical verification, was carried out with the assistance of a large language model (LLM), under strict human oversight and independent numerical cross-checking. This division of labour enables the LLM to handle tedious symbolic manipulation without compromising rigour. Results are presented for spinning modes radiating from a cylindrical duct with a subsonic jet into a quiescent ambient. The case study demonstrates that, under systematic verification, LLMs can accelerate tedious algebra in theoretical fluid mechanics, contributing a concrete empirical example to the broader discussion on AI's role in theoretical research.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Kangjie Zhou, Sukai Wang, Yuhan Xiao, Qinghang Liu, Zhejia Wen

LeaP-VLN leverages progress both explicitly, through a progress verifier that verifies subtask completion before the agent advances and triggers dual-phase recovery upon route deviation, and implicitly, by co-training the executor on progress reasoning and action prediction to enhance the executor's progress awareness and corrective control. 具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) encode a high-resolution image into thousands of visual tokens, which dominate the cost of the prefill stage. In the first stage, a glance encoder views the image at low resolution and re-encodes only the question-relevant regions at native resolution. 具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Jiajun Sun, Zeyu Zhang, Zeyu Ren, Guangfeng Jiang, Yang Zhao
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: PanDWM introduces a panoramic 4D driving world model that enhances video generation efficiency and consistency by integrating multiple camera views into a continuous 360° image.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one $360^\circ$ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched $360^\circ$ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at $8$-$46\times$ their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Jiarui Dong, Zhiheng Liang, Yanjun Li, Zeyu Zhang, Heejeong Nam
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: JEPA4R enhances JEPA world models by enabling 4D point planning from depth-camera point clouds, achieving superior performance in robotic manipulation tasks and zero-shot real-world application.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. 具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Kuan Zhang, Zirong Chen
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: RISE-RL enhances open-ended reinforcement learning by selectively exploring trajectories based on missed rubric criteria, significantly improving performance across various benchmarks.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) for open-ended tasks is challenging because responses must satisfy multidimensional criteria without following a single correct generation trajectory. 具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: TARGO and TARGO-Net: Benchmarking Target-driven Object Grasping under Occlusions
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Yan Xia, Ran Ding, Ziyuan Qin, Guanqi Zhan, Kaichen Zhou

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Yuan Wei, Ying Wei

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Learning and Verifying Progress: Closed-Loop Agentic Planning with Progress-Enhanced Execution for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Navigation

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Glance, then Select: Evidence-Tempered Visual Token Selection for Extremely Compressed Multimodal LLMs
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuxuan Wang, Guangxiang Zhao, Yuxuan Tian, Yahui Han, Xinyu Tan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The Glance-ETD framework efficiently reduces visual tokens in multimodal large language models, maintaining high performance while significantly speeding up processing and improving token selection.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiajun Sun, Zeyu Zhang, Zeyu Ren, Guangfeng Jiang, Yang Zhao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: PanDWM introduces a panoramic 4D driving world model that enhances video generation efficiency and consistency by integrating multiple camera views into a continuous 360° image.

Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched $360^\circ$ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at $8$-$46\times$ their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiarui Dong, Zhiheng Liang, Yanjun Li, Zeyu Zhang, Heejeong Nam
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: JEPA4R enhances JEPA world models by enabling 4D point planning from depth-camera point clouds, achieving superior performance in robotic manipulation tasks and zero-shot real-world application.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. 情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Kuan Zhang, Zirong Chen
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: RISE-RL enhances open-ended reinforcement learning by selectively exploring trajectories based on missed rubric criteria, significantly improving performance across various benchmarks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) for open-ended tasks is challenging because responses must satisfy multidimensional criteria without following a single correct generation trajectory. These results indicate that selective internalization through reward filtering and policy support shaping is effective for open-ended reinforcement learning.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: TARGO and TARGO-Net: Benchmarking Target-driven Object Grasping under Occlusions
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yan Xia, Ran Ding, Ziyuan Qin, Guanqi Zhan, Kaichen Zhou
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces TARGO, a benchmark dataset for target-driven grasping under occlusions, and TARGO-Net, a robust model that improves grasp prediction accuracy in cluttered environments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Predicting 6-DoF grasp poses from a single RGB-D frame has recently achieved impressive accuracy, yet performance can degrade significantly when the target object is heavily occluded by clutter. 情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Yuan Wei, Ying Wei
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper explores how on-policy distillation reshapes interaction patterns in language-model agents across various domains, revealing both improvements and negative transfers in performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Passage-Focused Soft Coordination for Hierarchical Multi-Robot Navigation in Bottleneck Environments
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haoze Dong, Stepan Dergachev, Meng Guo, Konstantin Yakovlev, Zhongkui Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The proposed passage-focused framework enhances multi-robot navigation by integrating soft global coordination with flexible local execution, achieving high success rates and efficient collision avoidance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: In multi-robot navigation, rigid global schedules are sensitive to execution deviations, while local methods lack long-horizon coordination. A passage-induced graph of convex sets supports priority-ordered planning with two levels of soft coordination. Passage-aware route selection accounts for passage usage and traversal directions, while route-restricted continuous space-time planning penalizes temporal conflicts. The resulting references guide a model predictive path integral controller that avoids collisions online. Adaptive temporal and geometric tracking accommodates execution deviations, while selective replanning maintains coordination without rigid trajectory reservations. Hardware experiments with 8 robots demonstrate successful completion of all trials without collisions. These results highlight the effectiveness of passage-focused coordination in balancing long-horizon cooperation with flexible execution.

HMI Lab.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
HMI Lab.authors_text: Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen, Zekun Qi, Zekai Li
HMI Lab.summary: ScaleVLA, utilizing a 552B parameter backbone, enhances robot learning efficiency, generalization, and manipulation success compared to smaller Vision-Language-Action models.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

HMI Lab.title: DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
HMI Lab.authors_text: Hanlin Tian, Sihan Zhu, Zhao Yang, Yuxiang Wang, Zhiquan Hu
HMI Lab.summary: DetourBench introduces a trajectory-level evaluation framework for interactive agents, emphasizing minimum-action bounds to distinguish between efficient and inefficient decision-making processes.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Among recoverable failures, residual work separates near-complete trajectories from costly incompletion and from irreversible commitment. We open-source the instances, oracle witnesses, and evaluation harness at https://github.com/DatagridsAI/DetourBench.

HMI Lab.title: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
HMI Lab.authors_text: Fengmin Wu, Sicong Liu, Zimu Zhou, Chenren Xu, Wanbing Zhao
HMI Lab.summary: UbiHearo is a mobile assistant for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing users that provides scenario-aware sound guidance through a neuro-symbolic approach, enhancing situational awareness and personalized responses.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. In the first stage, a glance encoder views the image at low resolution and re-encodes only the question-relevant regions at native resolution. In the second stage, Evidence-Tempered Diversity (ETD) selects the final tokens by combining diversity with the evidence predicted by the scorer, so that the kept tokens cover the scene and retain the answer. A single-rollout self-distillation recipe trains the MLLM with the glance encoder. With only 5% of the visual tokens, Glance-ETD retains 91.6% of the full-token performance of Qwen3.5-4B across fourteen benchmarks and outperforms the strongest prior method, LT-OPD, by 17.3 points and the same training recipe with DivPrune by 6.0. It also speeds up the time to first token on 4K images by 3.1x and generalizes to three other MLLMs and to high-resolution document benchmarks, with the largest gains on text-rich tasks.

HMI Lab.title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
HMI Lab.authors_text: Jiajun Sun, Zeyu Zhang, Zeyu Ren, Guangfeng Jiang, Yang Zhao
HMI Lab.summary: PanDWM introduces a panoramic 4D driving world model that enhances video generation efficiency and consistency by integrating multiple camera views into a continuous 360° image.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one $360^\circ$ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched $360^\circ$ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at $8$-$46\times$ their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.

HMI Lab.title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
HMI Lab.authors_text: Jiarui Dong, Zhiheng Liang, Yanjun Li, Zeyu Zhang, Heejeong Nam
HMI Lab.summary: JEPA4R enhances JEPA world models by enabling 4D point planning from depth-camera point clouds, achieving superior performance in robotic manipulation tasks and zero-shot real-world application.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

HMI Lab.title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
HMI Lab.authors_text: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Kuan Zhang, Zirong Chen
HMI Lab.summary: RISE-RL enhances open-ended reinforcement learning by selectively exploring trajectories based on missed rubric criteria, significantly improving performance across various benchmarks.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) for open-ended tasks is challenging because responses must satisfy multidimensional criteria without following a single correct generation trajectory. Existing rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) methods compress fine-grained criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards, making persistent capability gaps difficult to target under limited on-policy exploration. We propose $\textbf{RISE-RL}$ (Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration), which uses repeatedly missed rubric criteria to elicit privileged trajectories that are difficult to discover through unguided exploration alone. RISE-RL retains only trajectories whose complete-rubric reward exceeds the mean reward of natural rollouts, and then re-evaluates them under the original prompt to emphasize behaviors that remain weakly supported by the natural policy. The resulting guidance signal is optimized through a separate auxiliary objective and removed once its additional benefit diminishes. Experiments with 4B and 14B models across writing, chat, health, and science show that RISE-RL achieves the highest mean score on every evaluated benchmark under guidance-free evaluation. Compared with standard Rubric-RL, it improves the average score by 1.3 points at the 4B scale and $\textbf{3.3 points at the 14B scale}$, including a $\textbf{6.0-point}$ gain on CreativeWriting-V3. It also improves creative-writing diversity and yields gains on objectively scored medical and scientific benchmarks. These results indicate that selective internalization through reward filtering and policy support shaping is effective for open-ended reinforcement learning.

HMI Lab.title: TARGO and TARGO-Net: Benchmarking Target-driven Object Grasping under Occlusions
HMI Lab.authors_text: Yan Xia, Ran Ding, Ziyuan Qin, Guanqi Zhan, Kaichen Zhou
HMI Lab.summary: The paper introduces TARGO, a benchmark dataset for target-driven grasping under occlusions, and TARGO-Net, a robust model that improves grasp prediction accuracy in cluttered environments.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Predicting 6-DoF grasp poses from a single RGB-D frame has recently achieved impressive accuracy, yet performance can degrade significantly when the target object is heavily occluded by clutter. In this paper, we establish TARGO, the first benchmark dataset for TARget-driven Grasping under Occlusions, and introduce TARGO-Net, a grasp prediction model designed for visual occlusion. Our main contributions are fourfold: 1) We identify the visual occlusion challenge in single-view RGB-D 6-DoF grasping and show that current state-of-the-art models still suffer under severe occlusion. 2) We propose the TARGO dataset, which supports training and testing 6-DoF grasp models across different visual occlusion levels and enables robustness evaluation in real-world scenarios. 3) We devise TARGO-Net, a transformer-based grasping model with a target completion module and target-scene cross-attention, which achieves the most robust performance across all visual occlusion levels. 4) We show that target completion, number of occluders, and target minimum dimension also relate to grasp success in addition to visual occlusion.

HMI Lab.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
HMI Lab.authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Yuan Wei, Ying Wei
HMI Lab.summary: The paper explores how on-policy distillation reshapes interaction patterns in language-model agents across various domains, revealing both improvements and negative transfers in performance.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

HMI Lab.title: Passage-Focused Soft Coordination for Hierarchical Multi-Robot Navigation in Bottleneck Environments
HMI Lab.authors_text: Haoze Dong, Stepan Dergachev, Meng Guo, Konstantin Yakovlev, Zhongkui Li
HMI Lab.summary: The proposed passage-focused framework enhances multi-robot navigation by integrating soft global coordination with flexible local execution, achieving high success rates and efficient collision avoidance.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: In multi-robot navigation, rigid global schedules are sensitive to execution deviations, while local methods lack long-horizon coordination. We propose a passage-focused framework combining soft global coordination with flexible local execution. A passage-induced graph of convex sets supports priority-ordered planning with two levels of soft coordination. Passage-aware route selection accounts for passage usage and traversal directions, while route-restricted continuous space-time planning penalizes temporal conflicts. The resulting references guide a model predictive path integral controller that avoids collisions online. Adaptive temporal and geometric tracking accommodates execution deviations, while selective replanning maintains coordination without rigid trajectory reservations. Across 1,200 instances in 4 different environments with 5-30 robots, the framework achieves a near-perfect success rate and outperforms evaluated baselines in makespan and flowtime. Hardware experiments with 8 robots demonstrate successful completion of all trials without collisions. These results highlight the effectiveness of passage-focused coordination in balancing long-horizon cooperation with flexible execution.

Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).title: SG-ODOM: Event-Driven Proprioceptive State Estimation with Stability-Gated Contact Updates for Legged Robots
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).authors_text: Francesco Iotti, Chiyun Noh, Franco Angelini, Manolo Garabini, Ayoung Kim
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).summary: SG-ODOM enhances proprioceptive state estimation in legged robots by using stability-gated contact updates to improve accuracy and reduce errors during dynamic movements.
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).debug_abstract: Reliable proprioceptive state estimation for legged robots fuses inertial sensing with kinematic sensing from leg encoders. The latter assumes a foot is stationary during the stance phase; however, physical foot touchdown does not necessarily provide a stationary reference for odometry, particularly during impact and load transfer. Repeatedly applying kinematic corrections throughout the same contact phase can introduce redundant or unreliable information. We present SG-ODOM, a proprioceptive odometry framework that uses stability-gated contact selection to schedule kinematic updates. Following physical touchdown, a stability gate accepts the contact for state estimation only after the foot reaches a sufficiently stable support condition. The resulting validated touchdown event triggers an estimator correction, while additional timeout updates bound the maximum duration of uninterrupted IMU propagation. The framework is evaluated on multiple legged platforms, both quadrupedal and humanoid robots, against representative state-of-the-art proprioceptive estimators. Across the evaluated sequences, SG-ODOM demonstrates competitive or superior estimation accuracy, reducing Relative Pose Error (RPE) by up to 25% compared to the baseline estimator on outdoor sequences from the GrandTour dataset. Source code: https://github.com/ori-drs/SG-ODOM. Video: https://youtu.be/-583_RyuhqQ

Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).title: DeepfakeBench-MM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).authors_text: Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yupeng Chen, Yize Chen, Weinan Guan
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).summary: The paper presents DeepfakeBench-MM, a benchmark for multimodal deepfake detection using the Mega-MMDF dataset, enhancing training and evaluation across diverse forgery techniques and detectors.
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).debug_abstract: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.

Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).title: TARGO and TARGO-Net: Benchmarking Target-driven Object Grasping under Occlusions
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).authors_text: Yan Xia, Ran Ding, Ziyuan Qin, Guanqi Zhan, Kaichen Zhou
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).summary: The paper introduces TARGO, a benchmark dataset for target-driven grasping under occlusions, and TARGO-Net, a robust model that improves grasp prediction accuracy in cluttered environments.
