Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).title: CISyn: Human Mesh Recovery in Close Interactions with Physics-Simulated Synthetic Data
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).authors_text: Yufan Deng, Lorenza Prospero, Christian Rupprecht
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).summary: CISyn is a synthetic dataset for 3D human mesh recovery in close interactions, utilizing physics simulation to produce realistic contact and occlusion without manual annotation.
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).debug_abstract: 3D human mesh recovery (HMR) in close-interaction scenarios is hindered by the lack of large-scale, accurately annotated training data: real capture is expensive, and existing synthetic datasets rarely include physical contact. We introduce CISyn, a large-scale synthetic dataset purpose-built for close human-human interactions, generated via physics simulation and Blender-based rendering. By simulating collision dynamics between SMPL-X-rigged humanoids, CISyn naturally produces the contact, mutual occlusion, and pose entanglement that characterize close-interaction scenes, with no manual annotation effort. The released set provides 25,000 sequences with accurate 3D annotations. We further propose an uncertainty-aware loss that allows models to learn more effectively from the heavily occluded examples in our data. Augmenting state-of-the-art HMR training with CISyn and replacing the regression loss with our uncertainty-aware variant yields consistent improvements on close-interaction benchmarks, validating CISyn as a scalable complement to real-world data. The dataset, generation pipeline, and code are available at https://github.com/yfde/CISyn.

浙江大学.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
浙江大学.authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He
浙江大学.summary: Ego-CEVR is a framework that enhances robot learning by leveraging egocentric videos through distinct global and interaction representation objectives, achieving superior performance and generalization.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Egocentric videos offer a low-cost, scalable source of manipulation experience for robot learning. However, existing methods often fail to tailor their use of egocentric videos and robot demonstrations to the differences in their formats and information content. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns task context through future video prediction, while the interaction module uses this context to interpret wrist observations and learns local execution information through robot action supervision. The distinct learning objectives enable independent pretraining on large-scale human and robot egocentric videos to learn task context, and training on real-robot demonstrations to align the learned representations with fine-grained robot actions. Experiments show leading performance on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, while real-robot evaluations demonstrate generalization across tasks and embodiments.

浙江大学.title: Perceive-to-Reason: Decoupling Perception and Reasoning for Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning
浙江大学.authors_text: Hongxing Li, Xiufeng Huang, Dingming Li, Wenjing Jiang, Zixuan Wang
浙江大学.summary: The Perceive-to-Reason (P2R) framework decouples perception and reasoning in visual tasks, enhancing performance through a two-stage process and a novel reinforcement learning strategy.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Fine-grained visual reasoning remains challenging for vision-language models, especially when small but critical visual cues are buried in high-resolution images. Existing approaches rely on repeated cropping or test-time visual search to introduce local evidence, but they typically do not explicitly distinguish perception from reasoning. In this paper, we propose Perceive-to-Reason (P2R), a unified framework that formulates fine-grained visual reasoning as a two-stage process: the model first localizes question-relevant evidence as a Perceiver, and then answers the question as a Reasoner based on the annotated image and cropped regions. To better align training with this decoupled formulation, we further introduce Perception-Reasoning Alternating GRPO (PRA-GRPO), a role-aware reinforcement learning strategy that alternates between perception-focused and reasoning-focused updates using only final-answer supervision. Built on top of Qwen3-VL-Instruct-2B/4B/8B, P2R consistently improves performance across model scales. In particular, P2R-4B achieves 93.2% on V-Star, 81.9% on HR-Bench-4K, and 80.5% on HR-Bench-8K, substantially outperforming its corresponding backbone. Further experiments show that the benefits of P2R extend beyond high-resolution benchmarks to broader multimodal reasoning tasks. These results suggest that explicitly decoupling perception from reasoning provides an effective framework for fine-grained visual reasoning.

浙江大学.title: HINT: Human-Intent Inception for Agentic Robot Manipulation
浙江大学.authors_text: Mingyu Mei, Haojie Xu, Shihao Jin, Zibo Dai, Qihao Cheng
浙江大学.summary: HINT is a framework that enhances robot manipulation by aligning semantic intent with evolving visual inputs, improving task success and intent understanding without extra training parameters.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Humans can perform complex manipulations given a simple intent through an overall instruction, while continuously adapting to evolving visual observations. However, current vision-language action (VLA) models and other action policies struggle to realize this high-level intelligent behavior under dense, evolving visual inputs and sparse language guidance. Visual correlations can then dominate semantic intent, leading actions to follow visual shortcuts rather than human goals. We present HINT (Human-INTent INcepTion), an agentic framework inspired by the human manipulation principles: semantic intent changes sparsely at manipulation-pattern transitions, whereas continuous control primarily depends on the evolving object-hand relationship. HINT invokes semantic reasoning only at pattern transitions to resolve the current subtask and target, then maintains this commitment through multi-view grounding and visual tracking. We explore two visual interfaces-image-space semantic highlighting and attention-prior injection-to communicate the tracked intent to the action policy without introducing additional trainable parameters into the foundation action model. Experiments across three long-horizon tasks and out-of-distribution variants show that HINT substantially improves intent understanding, task progress, and end-to-end success across two foundation policies while preserving low-latency control. Project page: https://robot-hint.github.io/

浙江大学.title: SkillBoost: A Constrained Exploration-Exploitation Process for Mitigating Skill Overfitting
浙江大学.authors_text: Hongqiang Lin, Chao Liu, Xiaofan Bai, Xuan Jin, Yuhong Li
浙江大学.summary: SkillBoost is a three-stage framework that optimizes skill self-evolution in LLM agents, balancing exploration and exploitation to mitigate overfitting and enhance performance.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Enabling large language model (LLM) agents to accumulate and reuse experience from past interactions remains a central challenge in real-world applications. A promising solution is to treat skills as trainable states and optimize them in the same way as model parameters in neural network training. However, data-driven skill optimization is prone to overfitting to the limited trajectories collected from real environments. Overexploiting these trajectories overfits the current batch, while unconstrained exploration causes regression on previously solved cases. This tension motivates a constrained search view of skill self-evolution, governed by an exploration--exploitation trade-off. We propose SkillBoost, a three-stage framework that mitigates both risks: structured exploitation localizes observed failures to editable skill components, prior-guided exploration draws on prior knowledge in the LLM to generate diverse repair candidates, and verified acceptance commits a candidate only when it improves performance within a regression bound. Experiments across 23 model--benchmark configurations show that SkillBoost achieves state-of-the-art performance while mitigating overfitting, outperforming both human-crafted and LLM-generated skills. Transfer experiments further show that optimized skills can be reused by other agents on similar tasks. The code is available at https://github.com/HQ-Lin/SkillBoost

浙江大学.title: Seeing but Not Thinking: Routing Distraction in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts
浙江大学.authors_text: Haolei Xu, Haiwen Hong, Hongxing Li, Rui Zhou, Yang Zhang
浙江大学.summary: The paper identifies a "Seeing but Not Thinking" phenomenon in MoE models, revealing routing distraction during visual input processing that hinders reasoning, and proposes interventions to enhance expert activation.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have achieved remarkable performance on vision-language tasks. However, we identify a puzzling phenomenon termed Seeing but Not Thinking: models accurately perceive image content yet fail in subsequent reasoning, while correctly solving identical problems presented as pure text. Through systematic analysis, we first verify that cross-modal semantic sharing exists in MoE architectures, ruling out semantic alignment failure as the sole explanation. We then reveal that visual experts and domain experts exhibit layer-wise separation, with image inputs inducing significant routing divergence from text inputs in middle layers where domain experts concentrate. Based on these findings, we propose the Routing Distraction hypothesis: when processing visual inputs, the routing mechanism fails to adequately activate task-relevant reasoning experts. To validate this hypothesis, we design a routing-guided intervention method that enhances domain expert activation. Experiments on three multimodal MoE models across six benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements, with gains of up to 3.17% on complex visual reasoning tasks. Our analysis further reveals that domain expert identification locates cognitive functions rather than sample-specific solutions, enabling effective transfer across tasks with different information structures.

浙江大学.title: DiffWAM: Learning World Action Model from Consecutive Visual Difference
浙江大学.authors_text: Xinheng Zhang, Haoyu Xiong, Chao Jing, Xiaohan Zhang, Linshan Li
浙江大学.summary: DiffWAM introduces a Mixture-of-Experts framework that enhances robot learning by predicting future states and actions through consecutive visual differences, achieving state-of-the-art performance in manipulation tasks.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as an important paradigm in robot learning, jointly predicting future scene states and robot actions from current observations and instructions. However, future states entangle task-related changes with large amounts of task-irrelevant content, such as static backgrounds, which weakens the model's ability to capture changes relevant to task execution. To address this, we propose Difference World Action Model (DiffWAM), a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework that enhances world representations by jointly learning future-state prediction and consecutive visual difference prediction. We define consecutive visual differences as differences between the latent representations of consecutive observations, providing an explicit learning signal for temporal variation. The framework comprises a World Expert for future frame prediction, an Action Expert for action generation, and a Diff Expert for predicting these latent differences along the trajectory. A structured unidirectional attention mask conditions the Diff, World, and Action Experts solely on the current-frame representation while blocking attention between experts. This design allows both the World and Diff Experts to be removed during inference, introducing no additional inference overhead. DiffWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on the LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks and substantially improves over FastWAM on real-world manipulation tasks. Specifically, it attains average success rates of 98.8%, 92.65%, and 88.3%, outperforming the state-of-the-art baseline (i.e., FastWAM) by 1.75, 1.55, and 15.0 percentage points, respectively.

浙江大学.title: DeformMaster: An Interactive Physics-Neural World Model for Deformable Objects from Videos
浙江大学.authors_text: Can Li, Zhoujian Li, Ren Li, Jie Gu, Lei Lei
浙江大学.summary: DeformMaster is an advanced interactive physics-neural model that accurately simulates and visualizes the dynamics of deformable objects using real video data.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: World models for deformable objects should recover not only geometry and appearance, but also underlying physical dynamics, interaction grounding, and material behavior. Learning such a model from real videos is challenging because deformable linear, planar, and volumetric objects evolve under high-dimensional deformation, noisy interactions, and complex material response. The model must infer a physical state from visual observations, roll it forward under new interactions, and render the resulting dynamics with high visual fidelity. We therefore present DeformMaster, a video-derived interactive physics-neural world model that turns real interaction videos into an online interactive model of deformable objects within a unified dynamics-and-appearance framework. DeformMaster preserves structured physical rollout while using a neural residual to compensate for unmodeled effects, grounds sparse hand motion as distributed compliant actuators for hand-continuum interaction, represents material response with spatially varying constitutive experts, and drives high-fidelity 4D appearance from the predicted physical evolution. Experiments on real-world deformable-object sequences demonstrate DeformMaster's ability to roll out future dynamics and render dynamic appearance, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines while supporting novel action rollout, material-parameter variation, and dynamic novel-view synthesis. Code and video demos are available at the project page: https://can-lee.github.io/deformmaster-web/

浙江大学.title: USER: A Unified and Extensible System for Online Real-World Policy Learning in Embodied AI
浙江大学.authors_text: Hongzhi Zang, Shu'ang Yu, Hao Lin, Tianxing Zhou, Zefang Huang
浙江大学.summary: USER is a unified system that enhances online real-world policy learning in embodied AI through hardware abstraction, adaptive communication, and asynchronous training frameworks.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Online policy learning directly in the physical world is a promising yet challenging direction for embodied intelligence. Unlike simulation, real-world systems cannot be arbitrarily accelerated, cheaply reset, or massively replicated, suggesting that real-world policy learning is not merely an algorithmic problem, but inherently a systems problem. We present \user, a \underline{U}nified and extensible \underline{S}yst\underline{E}m for online real-world policy lea\underline{R}ning. On the systems side, \user introduces a hardware abstraction layer for unified robot management and an adaptive communication plane that enables efficient cloud-edge training. On the learning side, \user adopts a fully asynchronous training framework, designs a persistent and cache-aware replay buffer, and provides extensible abstractions for rewards, algorithms, and policies. Experiments in both simulation and the real world demonstrate that \user supports multi-robot coordination, heterogeneous manipulators, cloud-edge training with large models, and long-running asynchronous training. Together, these capabilities establish \user as a unified and extensible systems foundation for online real-world policy learning.

浙江大学.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
浙江大学.authors_text: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Yuan Wei, Ying Wei

浙江大学.title: DecoEdit: Beyond Flat Control for 3D-Aware Unified Image Editing
浙江大学.authors_text: Xiaotang Gai, Jinbo Xing, Zijie Meng, Jiayi Yi, Jimin Xiao
浙江大学.summary: DecoEdit introduces a unified framework for 3D-aware image editing, integrating multi-dimensional inputs and achieving superior geometric accuracy and identity preservation over existing models.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: While recent advances in multimodal image editing have achieved impressive results, current frameworks remain largely confined to ``flat" 2D controls (e.g., text prompts, bounding boxes, or masks). Precise 3D-aware geometric manipulation -- such as coordinating an object's location, physical scale, and 3D orientation while strictly preserving its fine-grained identity -- remains an elusive challenge, typically suffering from severe detail degradation or requiring expensive per-instance fine-tuning. In this paper, we present DecoEdit, an all-in-one image editing framework that goes beyond flat control by seamlessly integrating 1D textual, 2D spatial, and 3D volumetric inputs under a unified architecture. First, to power this unified model, we establish a data curation pipeline and curate a large-scale dataset, namely DecoDataset, containing 1.6 million samples, encompassing diverse multi-dimensional (1D/2D/3D) tasks and their complex compositions. Furthermore, we establish a comprehensive image editing benchmark named DecoBench to systematically evaluate multi-task editing performance. Finally, to address the fundamental trade-off between complex spatial transformations and identity preservation, we propose a novel decoupled pipeline: DecoEdit factorizes the editing process by utilizing structural guidance from SAM-3D to anchor the target geometry, scale, and spatial orientation, while concurrently leveraging a detail-preservation path to lock in high-fidelity textures. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecoEdit achieves state-of-the-art results. Notably, on the challenging 3D spatial pose and orientation control tasks, DecoEdit significantly outperforms leading closed-source models such as Seedream 5.0 in both geometric accuracy and identity consistency.

Rajpurkar Lab.title: ImpedanceMimic: Learned Impedance as Action Space for Force-Accurate Motion Imitation
Rajpurkar Lab.summary: ImpedanceMimic leverages reinforcement learning to optimize joint stiffness and damping for improved motion imitation, achieving superior force and motion fidelity across diverse activities and subjects.
Rajpurkar Lab.debug_abstract: Recovering the forces behind a motion is ill-posed: different controllers can reproduce the same movement while generating different contact forces. Physics-based motion imitation resolves this ambiguity through simulation, but relies on fixed-gain proportional-derivative (PD) control. We show that fixed gains impose a trade-off between motion and force tracking, as contact and swing place conflicting demands on joint stiffness and damping. We introduce ImpedanceMimic, a reinforcement-learning policy that modulates per-joint stiffness, damping, and position setpoints from motion and force measurements, but requires only motion at inference. Across 129 participants and six activities, ImpedanceMimic outperforms matched fixed-gain PD under every integration scheme, direct-torque, muscle-actuated and existing imitation controllers in kinematic and force fidelity, approaching a dedicated motion-to-force regressor. By expressing gains as multiples of inertia-scaled priors, a single policy controls subject-specific biomechanical models without explicit anthropometric input and transfers zero-shot to unseen humans and a humanoid robot. The learned impedance forms a low-dimensional representation of motor state, shared across bodies, that generalizes to withheld activities: stiffness scales with load, and damping anticipates unloading.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Yancheng Long, Xuanyu Zheng, Wei Chen, Luoyuan Zhang, Haoyang Xu
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: VideoNexus is a framework that enhances video understanding by decoupling perception from planning, achieving higher accuracy and efficiency in processing long videos.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. Even when relevant evidence is present, performing these operations within long, dense visual sequences burdens both perception and reasoning. Video agents enable selective inspection, but returning frames to the planner still accumulates visual information in its reasoning context. Delegating perception reduces this burden, yet sparse sampling can miss decisive details, and per-frame descriptions can preserve context growth. We introduce VideoNexus, a training-free framework that separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning. The planner controls where to inspect, what to resolve, and how densely to sample. Perception sub-agents process native audio-video in independent contexts and return compact, temporally grounded evidence for iterative search and verification. Using Gemini 3.8 Flash for both planning and perception, VideoNexus achieves 88.6% accuracy on full LVBench, exceeding same-backbone static ingestion and built-in agentic processing by 3.6 and 1.1 points, respectively, at 44% of the latter's measured API cost. A paired LVBench subset ablation shows lower planner input and higher accuracy. With Kimi K3 as the shared backbone, VideoNexus improves over the official Video-GAIA ReAct harness by 8.5 points in our evaluation. These results support compact evidence exchange for combining detailed observation with efficient planning and reasoning.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: DeepfakeBench-MM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yupeng Chen, Yize Chen, Weinan Guan
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: The paper presents DeepfakeBench-MM, a benchmark for multimodal deepfake detection using the Mega-MMDF dataset, enhancing training and evaluation across diverse forgery techniques and detectors.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: Ego-CEVR is a framework that enhances robot learning by leveraging egocentric videos through distinct global and interaction representation objectives, achieving superior performance and generalization.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: Egocentric videos offer a low-cost, scalable source of manipulation experience for robot learning. However, existing methods often fail to tailor their use of egocentric videos and robot demonstrations to the differences in their formats and information content. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns task context through future video prediction, while the interaction module uses this context to interpret wrist observations and learns local execution information through robot action supervision. The distinct learning objectives enable independent pretraining on large-scale human and robot egocentric videos to learn task context, and training on real-robot demonstrations to align the learned representations with fine-grained robot actions. Experiments show leading performance on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, while real-robot evaluations demonstrate generalization across tasks and embodiments.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: CtRoFlow: Monocular Camera-to-Robot Pose Estimation via Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: CtRoFlow introduces a novel flow matching framework for monocular camera-to-robot pose estimation, enhancing accuracy and robustness while addressing scale ambiguity and training complexity.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering, PnP based on predicted 2D keypoints with limited robustness or 3D registration which suffers from monocular scale ambiguity and complex training configuration. In this work, we propose CtRoFlow, a flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor (KFE) to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator (GCG), which generates condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-based Loss for decoupled training and scale consistency, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with multiple cameras, as well as for zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Code will be available upon acceptance.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: X-GS: An Extensible Framework for Perceiving and Thinking with 3D Gaussian Splatting
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Yueen Ma, Zenglin Xu, Irwin King
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: The X-GS framework integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting methods into a perception module for spatial AI, enhancing multimodal capabilities through improved SLAM and semantic distillation.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a powerful technique for novel view synthesis, subsequently extending into numerous spatial AI applications. However, most existing 3DGS methods operate in isolation, focusing on specific domains. In this paper, we introduce X-GS, an extensible framework that integrates previously isolated 3DGS methods into the perception module of a VLM for spatial tasks, with two major components: the $\textit{Perceiver}$ and the $\textit{Thinker}$. The $\textit{Perceiver}$ performs online 3DGS-based SLAM with semantic distillation and outputs semantic Gaussians from unposed video streams. It leverages recent vision foundation models for stronger geometric priors, and we introduce three novel optimizations to improve semantic distillation efficiency. The $\textit{Thinker}$ interfaces diverse VLMs with these semantic Gaussians, unlocking spatial multimodal capabilities such as 3D visual grounding and scene captioning. Experimental results on diverse benchmarks demonstrate the efficiency and newly unlocked multimodal capabilities of the X-GS framework. Code is available at https://github.com/yueen-ma/X-GS.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: 3D-MoE: Towards Spatial Intelligence with Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Reasoning and Action Generation
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Yueen Ma, Zenglin Xu, Irwin King
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: The 3D-MoE model enhances spatial intelligence by utilizing a mixture-of-experts architecture for efficient 3D reasoning and action generation in robotics.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence, encompassing 3D perception and reasoning, is the essential next frontier of AI. Scaling current 3D vision-language models (VLMs) that rely on dense Transformers for spatial tasks incurs prohibitive computational costs. In this paper, we introduce 3D-MoE, a 3D VLM leveraging an efficient mixture-of-experts architecture with a modality- and spatial-context-aware probabilistic routing scheme, stably cultivated by a novel routing curriculum. To seamlessly extend 3D-MoE to embodied AI, we integrate a diffusion-based action head, Pose-DiT, transforming 3D-MoE into a 3D vision-language-action (VLA) model. By employing a rectified flow framework, Pose-DiT generates precise 6D pose actions in a single sampling step. Extensive experiments demonstrate that 3D-MoE achieves superior performance on diverse 3D vision-language benchmarks with drastically fewer activated parameters and yields higher success rates while enabling real-time inference for robot manipulation tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/yueen-ma/3D-MoE.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Sen Shen, Ning Liu, Xiangrui Kong, Yingwei Li, Dongkun Han
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: This paper presents a reinforcement learning framework for autonomous vehicles that enhances socially compatible driving by integrating execution feedback to optimize interaction with human-driven vehicles.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) decisions at intersections affect the delay, braking, and motion smoothness of surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Learning socially compatible behavior requires connecting imagined interaction outcomes with feedback from executed actions. We propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden. An interaction-aware latent model supports imagination, while off-policy correction and replay updates enable observed rewards and transitions to supervise both the critic and actor. Simulation experiments at an unsignalized intersection achieve a 100% success and reductions in following-HDV acceleration variation of 65.5% and 44.0% relative to PIWM and DreamerV3, respectively. Ablations identify complementary roles for value calibration in reducing HDV burden and policy calibration in improving passage efficiency. Tests under out-of-distribution traffic shifts further show lower ego jerk and HDV acceleration variation than PIWM at comparable passage times.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: Calibrating the Uncertainty of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth without Labels
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: The paper introduces MonoCal, a method for calibrating the uncertainty of self-supervised monocular depth predictions, improving accuracy without requiring ground-truth depth data.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth networks can predict a per-pixel uncertainty, which is mainly evaluated by how well it ranks pixels according to their error. Such metrics are insensitive to the magnitude of the uncertainty, so an uncertainty half as large as the actual error obtains the same score. In this paper, we investigate whether the predicted uncertainty is as large as the depth error, both on average (scale) and across confident and uncertain, near and far pixels (shape). On KITTI, the scale is miscalibrated for every uncertainty estimate we evaluate, and the error of MonoProb is nearly twice its predicted uncertainty. We propose MonoCal, which corrects both the scale and the shape without ground-truth depth. Scale calibration multiplies the uncertainty by a single constant measured from stereo pairs, requiring no retraining, and this constant closely matches the one fitted with ground truth. Since a constant cannot change the shape, we further retrain the uncertainty to predict where the depth of the network disagrees with that of a second self-supervised network. Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges than rescaling with ground truth, while still using a single image at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Fengmin Wu, Sicong Liu, Zimu Zhou, Chenren Xu, Wanbing Zhao
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: UbiHearo is a mobile assistant for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing users that provides scenario-aware sound guidance through a neuro-symbolic approach, enhancing situational awareness and personalized responses.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. However, existing mobile assistants largely reduce acoustic scenes to isolated labels or generic alerts, failing to provide contextual guidance when the same sound implies different risks across scenarios. We present \sysname, a mobile hearing assistant agent that closes the sensing--reasoning--action loop for \textit{scenario-aware} and \textit{personalized} DHH assistance. \sysname adopts a \textit{neuro-symbolic} design that transforms continuous acoustic and physical context streams into structured intermediate representations (IRs) for controllable reasoning and guidance. It introduces three key mechanisms. \textit{First}, a perception-thresholded sensing mechanism enables energy-efficient always-on awareness by activating processing only for perceptually meaningful events while preserving safety-critical cues through deterministic overrides. \textit{Second}, a staged neuro-symbolic reasoning framework performs promptless scenario understanding by conditioning an on-device audio-language model on structured IRs instead of user-authored context descriptions. \textit{Third}, a bounded human-in-the-loop personalization mechanism adapts user-specific guidance through lightweight on-device decision-boundary updates while preserving population-aligned reasoning. We evaluate \sysname on smartphones and in-vehicle systems across diverse scenarios. It achieves favorable accuracy--latency--energy tradeoffs and personalized guidance.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yimin Han, Jiahui Zhang, Wanyue Li, Zeren Luo, Yeke Chen
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: MoViC enables real-time humanoid robot control from monocular video by integrating motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based model for dynamic task execution.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. Project page: https://movicproject.github.io/ .

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: MAPS: A Multimodal Agentic Framework for POI Data Production Based on Crowdsourced Street-view Imagery
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Sijie Ruan, Tingyu Xie, Mingfei Liu, Yicheng Tang, Haoyu Han
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: MAPS is a novel framework that enhances point-of-interest data production from crowdsourced street-view imagery, significantly improving accuracy and processing efficiency in urban database maintenance.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Point-of-interest (POI) databases support location-based services, yet urban changes quickly make their records stale and manual maintenance is costly. Crowdsourced street-view images provide timely visual evidence, but converting them into database actions requires separating multiple POIs and irrelevant text in each image, then resolving incomplete observations against ambiguous records. We study Street-view Image-based POI Data Production and propose MAPS, the first framework to integrate structured POI extraction with database maintenance from such imagery. MAPS contains two cascaded modules. SPICE progressively adapts a lightweight vision-language model to reconstruct and filter text, group entries belonging to the same POI, and classify their semantics and completeness. RIMA retrieves candidate records, performs evidence-grounded POI matching and attribute-level reasoning, and selectively acquires complementary visual, geospatial, or external-source evidence when necessary. In human-reviewed full-task evaluation, MAPS outperforms the strongest baseline by 21.8\%. MAPS has also been deployed in Kuaishou's large-scale POI production pipeline, reducing average processing time by 76.9\% relative to manual annotation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and practical value of MAPS for scalable POI maintenance.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: DeepfakeBench-MM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yupeng Chen, Yize Chen, Weinan Guan
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper presents DeepfakeBench-MM, a benchmark for multimodal deepfake detection using the Mega-MMDF dataset, enhancing training and evaluation across diverse forgery techniques and detectors.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: WinDEX: Metric 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild for Dexterous Teleoperation and Policy Learning
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Hongyu Ma, Hairong Qu, Shiqi Zhao, Yongsong Yang, Kai Shi
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: WinDEX introduces a novel method for metric 3D hand motion reconstruction using geometric-temporal optimization and advanced neural networks, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and real-time teleoperation capabilities.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Human manipulation data are widely used to train robots for human-like dexterity. However, low-cost, large-scale collection in the wild remains challenging. Existing methods remain limited in geometrically grounded metric-scale reconstruction, real-world generalization and inference speed. We present WinDEX, integrating (1) geometric-temporal optimization for metric 3D hand annotation from in-the-wild egocentric stereo videos, combined with visual-inertial SLAM for world-frame reconstruction; (2) WinDEX-Net, an end-to-end, fisheye-native network combining calibrated stereo, local detail and temporal context, with a data-model flywheel of model-assisted annotation and retraining; (3) distilled models for offline reconstruction and causal streaming, supporting reinforcement learning and teleoperation; and (4) low-cost CyberCap stereo-inertial capture, forming the WinDEX-Hand dataset with 1,000 hours of training annotations and held-out human-annotated in-the-wild 2D and independent optical motion-capture evaluation sets. Offline reconstruction runs at 43.61 FPS and causal streaming at 171 FPS. On held-out data, offline reconstruction achieves state-of-the-art accuracy: 14.5 pixels in-the-wild reprojection error and, with visual-inertial odometry, 37.29 mm world-frame joint error. We achieve 7.6 and 3.6 times the task success rates of reinforcement learning policies trained with WiLoR and HaWoR motion references, respectively, and demonstrate real-time arm-hand teleoperation. Project website: https://fruitrabbit.github.io/WinDEX/.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Ego-CEVR is a framework that enhances robot learning by leveraging egocentric videos through distinct global and interaction representation objectives, achieving superior performance and generalization.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Egocentric videos offer a low-cost, scalable source of manipulation experience for robot learning. However, existing methods often fail to tailor their use of egocentric videos and robot demonstrations to the differences in their formats and information content. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns task context through future video prediction, while the interaction module uses this context to interpret wrist observations and learns local execution information through robot action supervision. The distinct learning objectives enable independent pretraining on large-scale human and robot egocentric videos to learn task context, and training on real-robot demonstrations to align the learned representations with fine-grained robot actions. Experiments show leading performance on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, while real-robot evaluations demonstrate generalization across tasks and embodiments.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: CtRoFlow: Monocular Camera-to-Robot Pose Estimation via Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: CtRoFlow introduces a novel flow matching framework for monocular camera-to-robot pose estimation, enhancing accuracy and robustness while addressing scale ambiguity and training complexity.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering, PnP based on predicted 2D keypoints with limited robustness or 3D registration which suffers from monocular scale ambiguity and complex training configuration. In this work, we propose CtRoFlow, a flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor (KFE) to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator (GCG), which generates condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-based Loss for decoupled training and scale consistency, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with multiple cameras, as well as for zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Code will be available upon acceptance.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: X-GS: An Extensible Framework for Perceiving and Thinking with 3D Gaussian Splatting
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yueen Ma, Zenglin Xu, Irwin King
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The X-GS framework integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting methods into a perception module for spatial AI, enhancing multimodal capabilities through improved SLAM and semantic distillation.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a powerful technique for novel view synthesis, subsequently extending into numerous spatial AI applications. However, most existing 3DGS methods operate in isolation, focusing on specific domains. In this paper, we introduce X-GS, an extensible framework that integrates previously isolated 3DGS methods into the perception module of a VLM for spatial tasks, with two major components: the $\textit{Perceiver}$ and the $\textit{Thinker}$. The $\textit{Perceiver}$ performs online 3DGS-based SLAM with semantic distillation and outputs semantic Gaussians from unposed video streams. It leverages recent vision foundation models for stronger geometric priors, and we introduce three novel optimizations to improve semantic distillation efficiency. The $\textit{Thinker}$ interfaces diverse VLMs with these semantic Gaussians, unlocking spatial multimodal capabilities such as 3D visual grounding and scene captioning. Experimental results on diverse benchmarks demonstrate the efficiency and newly unlocked multimodal capabilities of the X-GS framework. Code is available at https://github.com/yueen-ma/X-GS.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: 3D-MoE: Towards Spatial Intelligence with Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Reasoning and Action Generation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yueen Ma, Zenglin Xu, Irwin King
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The 3D-MoE model enhances spatial intelligence by utilizing a mixture-of-experts architecture for efficient 3D reasoning and action generation in robotics.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence, encompassing 3D perception and reasoning, is the essential next frontier of AI. Scaling current 3D vision-language models (VLMs) that rely on dense Transformers for spatial tasks incurs prohibitive computational costs. In this paper, we introduce 3D-MoE, a 3D VLM leveraging an efficient mixture-of-experts architecture with a modality- and spatial-context-aware probabilistic routing scheme, stably cultivated by a novel routing curriculum. To seamlessly extend 3D-MoE to embodied AI, we integrate a diffusion-based action head, Pose-DiT, transforming 3D-MoE into a 3D vision-language-action (VLA) model. By employing a rectified flow framework, Pose-DiT generates precise 6D pose actions in a single sampling step. Extensive experiments demonstrate that 3D-MoE achieves superior performance on diverse 3D vision-language benchmarks with drastically fewer activated parameters and yields higher success rates while enabling real-time inference for robot manipulation tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/yueen-ma/3D-MoE.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Sen Shen, Ning Liu, Xiangrui Kong, Yingwei Li, Dongkun Han
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: This paper presents a reinforcement learning framework for autonomous vehicles that enhances socially compatible driving by integrating execution feedback to optimize interaction with human-driven vehicles.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) decisions at intersections affect the delay, braking, and motion smoothness of surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Learning socially compatible behavior requires connecting imagined interaction outcomes with feedback from executed actions. We propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden. An interaction-aware latent model supports imagination, while off-policy correction and replay updates enable observed rewards and transitions to supervise both the critic and actor. Simulation experiments at an unsignalized intersection achieve a 100% success and reductions in following-HDV acceleration variation of 65.5% and 44.0% relative to PIWM and DreamerV3, respectively. Ablations identify complementary roles for value calibration in reducing HDV burden and policy calibration in improving passage efficiency. Tests under out-of-distribution traffic shifts further show lower ego jerk and HDV acceleration variation than PIWM at comparable passage times.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: MoRAE: Flow-Friendly Self-Supervised Latents for Text-to-Motion Generation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yifei Zhu, Dafei Qin, Zijiao Zeng, Mingyi Shi, Yangyang Cai
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: MoRAE introduces a self-supervised motion representation for text-to-motion generation that outperforms traditional methods by compressing predictive features into a reliable latent space.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Which latent space should a text-to-motion generator model? We show that a self-supervised motion representation, once compressed, is a better generative space than latents learned by reconstruction. Our approach, MoRAE, is simple: we pre-train a Motion-JEPA encoder that predicts hidden joint trajectories from the rest of the body, and compress its frozen features into a compact latent for a standard flow transformer. Two observations drive this design. First, prediction yields features that capture action semantics and cross-joint structure better than reconstruction. Second, these features are ill-conditioned, and a standard flow transformer generates poorly in them directly. Compressing them into a compact latent makes generation reliable and places cross-joint structure on the directions the flow models most accurately. With a 58M DiT and the standard CLIP text condition, MoRAE achieves state-of-the-art FID on HumanML3D and KIT-ML while maintaining retrieval-based text consistency and diversity close to real motion.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Calibrating the Uncertainty of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth without Labels
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper introduces MonoCal, a method for calibrating the uncertainty of self-supervised monocular depth predictions, improving accuracy without requiring ground-truth depth data.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth networks can predict a per-pixel uncertainty, which is mainly evaluated by how well it ranks pixels according to their error. Such metrics are insensitive to the magnitude of the uncertainty, so an uncertainty half as large as the actual error obtains the same score. In this paper, we investigate whether the predicted uncertainty is as large as the depth error, both on average (scale) and across confident and uncertain, near and far pixels (shape). On KITTI, the scale is miscalibrated for every uncertainty estimate we evaluate, and the error of MonoProb is nearly twice its predicted uncertainty. We propose MonoCal, which corrects both the scale and the shape without ground-truth depth. Scale calibration multiplies the uncertainty by a single constant measured from stereo pairs, requiring no retraining, and this constant closely matches the one fitted with ground truth. Since a constant cannot change the shape, we further retrain the uncertainty to predict where the depth of the network disagrees with that of a second self-supervised network. Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges than rescaling with ground truth, while still using a single image at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yancheng Long, Xuanyu Zheng, Wei Chen, Luoyuan Zhang, Haoyang Xu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: VideoNexus is a framework that enhances video understanding by decoupling perception from planning, achieving higher accuracy and efficiency in processing long videos.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. Even when relevant evidence is present, performing these operations within long, dense visual sequences burdens both perception and reasoning. Video agents enable selective inspection, but returning frames to the planner still accumulates visual information in its reasoning context. Delegating perception reduces this burden, yet sparse sampling can miss decisive details, and per-frame descriptions can preserve context growth. We introduce VideoNexus, a training-free framework that separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning. The planner controls where to inspect, what to resolve, and how densely to sample. Perception sub-agents process native audio-video in independent contexts and return compact, temporally grounded evidence for iterative search and verification. Using Gemini 3.8 Flash for both planning and perception, VideoNexus achieves 88.6% accuracy on full LVBench, exceeding same-backbone static ingestion and built-in agentic processing by 3.6 and 1.1 points, respectively, at 44% of the latter's measured API cost. A paired LVBench subset ablation shows lower planner input and higher accuracy. With Kimi K3 as the shared backbone, VideoNexus improves over the official Video-GAIA ReAct harness by 8.5 points in our evaluation. These results support compact evidence exchange for combining detailed observation with efficient planning and reasoning.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: Ego-CEVR is a framework that enhances robot learning by leveraging egocentric videos through distinct global and interaction representation objectives, achieving superior performance and generalization.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Egocentric videos offer a low-cost, scalable source of manipulation experience for robot learning. 机器人与自动化研究中心.title: CtRoFlow: Monocular Camera-to-Robot Pose Estimation via Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: CtRoFlow introduces a novel flow matching framework for monocular camera-to-robot pose estimation, enhancing accuracy and robustness while addressing scale ambiguity and training complexity.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. 机器人与自动化研究中心.title: X-GS: An Extensible Framework for Perceiving and Thinking with 3D Gaussian Splatting
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Yueen Ma, Zenglin Xu, Irwin King
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The X-GS framework integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting methods into a perception module for spatial AI, enhancing multimodal capabilities through improved SLAM and semantic distillation.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a powerful technique for novel view synthesis, subsequently extending into numerous spatial AI applications. The $\textit{Perceiver}$ performs online 3DGS-based SLAM with semantic distillation and outputs semantic Gaussians from unposed video streams. 机器人与自动化研究中心.title: 3D-MoE: Towards Spatial Intelligence with Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Reasoning and Action Generation
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Yueen Ma, Zenglin Xu, Irwin King
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The 3D-MoE model enhances spatial intelligence by utilizing a mixture-of-experts architecture for efficient 3D reasoning and action generation in robotics.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence, encompassing 3D perception and reasoning, is the essential next frontier of AI. Scaling current 3D vision-language models (VLMs) that rely on dense Transformers for spatial tasks incurs prohibitive computational costs. In this paper, we introduce 3D-MoE, a 3D VLM leveraging an efficient mixture-of-experts architecture with a modality- and spatial-context-aware probabilistic routing scheme, stably cultivated by a novel routing curriculum. To seamlessly extend 3D-MoE to embodied AI, we integrate a diffusion-based action head, Pose-DiT, transforming 3D-MoE into a 3D vision-language-action (VLA) model. By employing a rectified flow framework, Pose-DiT generates precise 6D pose actions in a single sampling step. Extensive experiments demonstrate that 3D-MoE achieves superior performance on diverse 3D vision-language benchmarks with drastically fewer activated parameters and yields higher success rates while enabling real-time inference for robot manipulation tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/yueen-ma/3D-MoE.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Sen Shen, Ning Liu, Xiangrui Kong, Yingwei Li, Dongkun Han
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: This paper presents a reinforcement learning framework for autonomous vehicles that enhances socially compatible driving by integrating execution feedback to optimize interaction with human-driven vehicles.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) decisions at intersections affect the delay, braking, and motion smoothness of surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Learning socially compatible behavior requires connecting imagined interaction outcomes with feedback from executed actions. We propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden. An interaction-aware latent model supports imagination, while off-policy correction and replay updates enable observed rewards and transitions to supervise both the critic and actor. Ablations identify complementary roles for value calibration in reducing HDV burden and policy calibration in improving passage efficiency. Tests under out-of-distribution traffic shifts further show lower ego jerk and HDV acceleration variation than PIWM at comparable passage times.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Calibrating the Uncertainty of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth without Labels
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The paper introduces MonoCal, a method for calibrating the uncertainty of self-supervised monocular depth predictions, improving accuracy without requiring ground-truth depth data.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth networks can predict a per-pixel uncertainty, which is mainly evaluated by how well it ranks pixels according to their error. Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges than rescaling with ground truth, while still using a single image at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

OpenDriveLab.title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams

OpenDriveLab.summary: MoViC enables real-time humanoid robot control from monocular video by integrating motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based model for dynamic task execution.

OpenDriveLab.title: MAPS: A Multimodal Agentic Framework for POI Data Production Based on Crowdsourced Street-view Imagery
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Sijie Ruan, Tingyu Xie, Mingfei Liu, Yicheng Tang, Haoyu Han
OpenDriveLab.summary: MAPS is a novel framework that enhances point-of-interest data production from crowdsourced street-view imagery, significantly improving accuracy and processing efficiency in urban database maintenance.
