OpenDriveLab.title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Sen Shen, Ning Liu, Xiangrui Kong, Yingwei Li, Dongkun Han
OpenDriveLab.summary: This paper presents a reinforcement learning framework for autonomous vehicles that enhances socially compatible driving by integrating execution feedback to optimize interaction with human-driven vehicles.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) decisions at intersections affect the delay, braking, and motion smoothness of surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Learning socially compatible behavior requires connecting imagined interaction outcomes with feedback from executed actions. We propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden. An interaction-aware latent model supports imagination, while off-policy correction and replay updates enable observed rewards and transitions to supervise both the critic and actor. Simulation experiments at an unsignalized intersection achieve a 100% success and reductions in following-HDV acceleration variation of 65.5% and 44.0% relative to PIWM and DreamerV3, respectively. Ablations identify complementary roles for value calibration in reducing HDV burden and policy calibration in improving passage efficiency. Tests under out-of-distribution traffic shifts further show lower ego jerk and HDV acceleration variation than PIWM at comparable passage times.

OpenDriveLab.title: MoRAE: Flow-Friendly Self-Supervised Latents for Text-to-Motion Generation
OpenDriveLab.authors_text: Yifei Zhu, Dafei Qin, Zijiao Zeng, Mingyi Shi, Yangyang Cai
OpenDriveLab.summary: MoRAE introduces a self-supervised motion representation for text-to-motion generation that outperforms traditional methods by compressing predictive features into a reliable latent space.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Which latent space should a text-to-motion generator model? We show that a self-supervised motion representation, once compressed, is a better generative space than latents learned by reconstruction. Our approach, MoRAE, is simple: we pre-train a Motion-JEPA encoder that predicts hidden joint trajectories from the rest of the body, and compress its frozen features into a compact latent for a standard flow transformer. Two observations drive this design. First, prediction yields features that capture action semantics and cross-joint structure better than reconstruction. Second, these features are ill-conditioned, and a standard flow transformer generates poorly in them directly. Compressing them into a compact latent makes generation reliable and places cross-joint structure on the directions the flow models most accurately. With a 58M DiT and the standard CLIP text condition, MoRAE achieves state-of-the-art FID on HumanML3D and KIT-ML while maintaining retrieval-based text consistency and diversity close to real motion.

OpenDriveLab.title: Calibrating the Uncertainty of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth without Labels
OpenDriveLab.summary: The paper introduces MonoCal, a method for calibrating the uncertainty of self-supervised monocular depth predictions, improving accuracy without requiring ground-truth depth data.
OpenDriveLab.debug_abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth networks can predict a per-pixel uncertainty, which is mainly evaluated by how well it ranks pixels according to their error. Such metrics are insensitive to the magnitude of the uncertainty, so an uncertainty half as large as the actual error obtains the same score. In this paper, we investigate whether the predicted uncertainty is as large as the depth error, both on average (scale) and across confident and uncertain, near and far pixels (shape). On KITTI, the scale is miscalibrated for every uncertainty estimate we evaluate, and the error of MonoProb is nearly twice its predicted uncertainty. We propose MonoCal, which corrects both the scale and the shape without ground-truth depth. Scale calibration multiplies the uncertainty by a single constant measured from stereo pairs, requiring no retraining, and this constant closely matches the one fitted with ground truth. Since a constant cannot change the shape, we further retrain the uncertainty to predict where the depth of the network disagrees with that of a second self-supervised network. Experiments on KITTI show that MonoCal achieves better calibration across uncertainty levels and depth ranges than rescaling with ground truth, while still using a single image at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yancheng Long, Xuanyu Zheng, Wei Chen, Luoyuan Zhang, Haoyang Xu
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: VideoNexus is a framework that enhances video understanding by decoupling perception from planning, achieving higher accuracy and efficiency in processing long videos.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. Even when relevant evidence is present, performing these operations within long, dense visual sequences burdens both perception and reasoning. Video agents enable selective inspection, but returning frames to the planner still accumulates visual information in its reasoning context. Delegating perception reduces this burden, yet sparse sampling can miss decisive details, and per-frame descriptions can preserve context growth. We introduce VideoNexus, a training-free framework that separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning. The planner controls where to inspect, what to resolve, and how densely to sample. Perception sub-agents process native audio-video in independent contexts and return compact, temporally grounded evidence for iterative search and verification. Using Gemini 3.8 Flash for both planning and perception, VideoNexus achieves 88.6% accuracy on full LVBench, exceeding same-backbone static ingestion and built-in agentic processing by 3.6 and 1.1 points, respectively, at 44% of the latter's measured API cost. A paired LVBench subset ablation shows lower planner input and higher accuracy. With Kimi K3 as the shared backbone, VideoNexus improves over the official Video-GAIA ReAct harness by 8.5 points in our evaluation. These results support compact evidence exchange for combining detailed observation with efficient planning and reasoning.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Fengmin Wu, Sicong Liu, Zimu Zhou, Chenren Xu, Wanbing Zhao
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: UbiHearo is a mobile assistant for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing users that provides scenario-aware sound guidance through a neuro-symbolic approach, enhancing situational awareness and personalized responses.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. However, existing mobile assistants largely reduce acoustic scenes to isolated labels or generic alerts, failing to provide contextual guidance when the same sound implies different risks across scenarios. We present \sysname, a mobile hearing assistant agent that closes the sensing--reasoning--action loop for \textit{scenario-aware} and \textit{personalized} DHH assistance. \sysname adopts a \textit{neuro-symbolic} design that transforms continuous acoustic and physical context streams into structured intermediate representations (IRs) for controllable reasoning and guidance. It introduces three key mechanisms. \textit{First}, a perception-thresholded sensing mechanism enables energy-efficient always-on awareness by activating processing only for perceptually meaningful events while preserving safety-critical cues through deterministic overrides. \textit{Second}, a staged neuro-symbolic reasoning framework performs promptless scenario understanding by conditioning an on-device audio-language model on structured IRs instead of user-authored context descriptions. \textit{Third}, a bounded human-in-the-loop personalization mechanism adapts user-specific guidance through lightweight on-device decision-boundary updates while preserving population-aligned reasoning. We evaluate \sysname on smartphones and in-vehicle systems across diverse scenarios. It achieves favorable accuracy--latency--energy tradeoffs and personalized guidance.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yimin Han, Jiahui Zhang, Wanyue Li, Zeren Luo, Yeke Chen
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: MoViC enables real-time humanoid robot control from monocular video by integrating motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based model for dynamic task execution.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. Project page: https://movicproject.github.io/ .

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: MAPS: A Multimodal Agentic Framework for POI Data Production Based on Crowdsourced Street-view Imagery
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Sijie Ruan, Tingyu Xie, Mingfei Liu, Yicheng Tang, Haoyu Han
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: MAPS is a novel framework that enhances point-of-interest data production from crowdsourced street-view imagery, significantly improving accuracy and processing efficiency in urban database maintenance.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Point-of-interest (POI) databases support location-based services, yet urban changes quickly make their records stale and manual maintenance is costly. Crowdsourced street-view images provide timely visual evidence, but converting them into database actions requires separating multiple POIs and irrelevant text in each image, then resolving incomplete observations against ambiguous records. We study Street-view Image-based POI Data Production and propose MAPS, the first framework to integrate structured POI extraction with database maintenance from such imagery. MAPS contains two cascaded modules. SPICE progressively adapts a lightweight vision-language model to reconstruct and filter text, group entries belonging to the same POI, and classify their semantics and completeness. RIMA retrieves candidate records, performs evidence-grounded POI matching and attribute-level reasoning, and selectively acquires complementary visual, geospatial, or external-source evidence when necessary. In human-reviewed full-task evaluation, MAPS outperforms the strongest baseline by 21.8\%. MAPS has also been deployed in Kuaishou's large-scale POI production pipeline, reducing average processing time by 76.9\% relative to manual annotation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and practical value of MAPS for scalable POI maintenance.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: DeepfakeBench-MM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yupeng Chen, Yize Chen, Weinan Guan
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The paper presents DeepfakeBench-MM, a benchmark for multimodal deepfake detection using the Mega-MMDF dataset, enhancing training and evaluation across diverse forgery techniques and detectors.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: WinDEX: Metric 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild for Dexterous Teleoperation and Policy Learning
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Hongyu Ma, Hairong Qu, Shiqi Zhao, Yongsong Yang, Kai Shi
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: WinDEX introduces a novel method for metric 3D hand motion reconstruction using geometric-temporal optimization and advanced neural networks, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and real-time teleoperation capabilities.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Human manipulation data are widely used to train robots for human-like dexterity. However, low-cost, large-scale collection in the wild remains challenging. Existing methods remain limited in geometrically grounded metric-scale reconstruction, real-world generalization and inference speed. We present WinDEX, integrating (1) geometric-temporal optimization for metric 3D hand annotation from in-the-wild egocentric stereo videos, combined with visual-inertial SLAM for world-frame reconstruction; (2) WinDEX-Net, an end-to-end, fisheye-native network combining calibrated stereo, local detail and temporal context, with a data-model flywheel of model-assisted annotation and retraining; (3) distilled models for offline reconstruction and causal streaming, supporting reinforcement learning and teleoperation; and (4) low-cost CyberCap stereo-inertial capture, forming the WinDEX-Hand dataset with 1,000 hours of training annotations and held-out human-annotated in-the-wild 2D and independent optical motion-capture evaluation sets. Offline reconstruction runs at 43.61 FPS and causal streaming at 171 FPS. On held-out data, offline reconstruction achieves state-of-the-art accuracy: 14.5 pixels in-the-wild reprojection error and, with visual-inertial odometry, 37.29 mm world-frame joint error. We achieve 7.6 and 3.6 times the task success rates of reinforcement learning policies trained with WiLoR and HaWoR motion references, respectively, and demonstrate real-time arm-hand teleoperation. Project website: https://fruitrabbit.github.io/WinDEX/.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: Ego-CEVR is a framework that enhances robot learning by leveraging egocentric videos through distinct global and interaction representation objectives, achieving superior performance and generalization.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Egocentric videos offer a low-cost, scalable source of manipulation experience for robot learning. However, existing methods often fail to tailor their use of egocentric videos and robot demonstrations to the differences in their formats and information content. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns task context through future video prediction, while the interaction module uses this context to interpret wrist observations and learns local execution information through robot action supervision. The distinct learning objectives enable independent pretraining on large-scale human and robot egocentric videos to learn task context, and training on real-robot demonstrations to align the learned representations with fine-grained robot actions. Experiments show leading performance on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, while real-robot evaluations demonstrate generalization across tasks and embodiments.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: CtRoFlow: Monocular Camera-to-Robot Pose Estimation via Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: CtRoFlow introduces a novel flow matching framework for monocular camera-to-robot pose estimation, enhancing accuracy and robustness while addressing scale ambiguity and training complexity.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering, PnP based on predicted 2D keypoints with limited robustness or 3D registration which suffers from monocular scale ambiguity and complex training configuration. In this work, we propose CtRoFlow, a flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor (KFE) to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator (GCG), which generates condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-based Loss for decoupled training and scale consistency, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with multiple cameras, as well as for zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Code will be available upon acceptance.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: X-GS: An Extensible Framework for Perceiving and Thinking with 3D Gaussian Splatting
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yueen Ma, Zenglin Xu, Irwin King
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The X-GS framework integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting methods into a perception module for spatial AI, enhancing multimodal capabilities through improved SLAM and semantic distillation.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a powerful technique for novel view synthesis, subsequently extending into numerous spatial AI applications. However, most existing 3DGS methods operate in isolation, focusing on specific domains. In this paper, we introduce X-GS, an extensible framework that integrates previously isolated 3DGS methods into the perception module of a VLM for spatial tasks, with two major components: the $\textit{Perceiver}$ and the $\textit{Thinker}$. The $\textit{Perceiver}$ performs online 3DGS-based SLAM with semantic distillation and outputs semantic Gaussians from unposed video streams. It leverages recent vision foundation models for stronger geometric priors, and we introduce three novel optimizations to improve semantic distillation efficiency. The $\textit{Thinker}$ interfaces diverse VLMs with these semantic Gaussians, unlocking spatial multimodal capabilities such as 3D visual grounding and scene captioning. Experimental results on diverse benchmarks demonstrate the efficiency and newly unlocked multimodal capabilities of the X-GS framework. Code is available at https://github.com/yueen-ma/X-GS.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: 3D-MoE: Towards Spatial Intelligence with Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Reasoning and Action Generation
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yueen Ma, Zenglin Xu, Irwin King
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The 3D-MoE model enhances spatial intelligence by utilizing a mixture-of-experts architecture for efficient 3D reasoning and action generation in robotics.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence, encompassing 3D perception and reasoning, is the essential next frontier of AI. Scaling current 3D vision-language models (VLMs) that rely on dense Transformers for spatial tasks incurs prohibitive computational costs. In this paper, we introduce 3D-MoE, a 3D VLM leveraging an efficient mixture-of-experts architecture with a modality- and spatial-context-aware probabilistic routing scheme, stably cultivated by a novel routing curriculum. To seamlessly extend 3D-MoE to embodied AI, we integrate a diffusion-based action head, Pose-DiT, transforming 3D-MoE into a 3D vision-language-action (VLA) model. By employing a rectified flow framework, Pose-DiT generates precise 6D pose actions in a single sampling step. Extensive experiments demonstrate that 3D-MoE achieves superior performance on diverse 3D vision-language benchmarks with drastically fewer activated parameters and yields higher success rates while enabling real-time inference for robot manipulation tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/yueen-ma/3D-MoE.

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He

Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.authors_text: Sen Shen, Ning Liu, Xiangrui Kong, Yingwei Li, Dongkun Han

潘佳老师实验室.title: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Fengmin Wu, Sicong Liu, Zimu Zhou, Chenren Xu, Wanbing Zhao
潘佳老师实验室.summary: UbiHearo is a mobile assistant for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing users that provides scenario-aware sound guidance through a neuro-symbolic approach, enhancing situational awareness and personalized responses.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. 潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yimin Han, Jiahui Zhang, Wanyue Li, Zeren Luo, Yeke Chen

潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Sijie Ruan, Tingyu Xie, Mingfei Liu, Yicheng Tang, Haoyu Han
潘佳老师实验室.summary: MAPS is a novel framework that enhances point-of-interest data production from crowdsourced street-view imagery, significantly improving accuracy and processing efficiency in urban database maintenance.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Point-of-interest (POI) databases support location-based services, yet urban changes quickly make their records stale and manual maintenance is costly.
