Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. Project page: https://movicproject.github.io/ .

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: Recovery-Guided Model-Based Diffusion for Safety-Critical Legged Locomotion
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Lei Zheng, Shivam Sood, Mithun Vanniasinghe, Guillaume Sartoretti, Armin Lederer
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: The proposed recovery-guided model-based diffusion framework enhances safety in high-speed legged locomotion by optimizing short-horizon trajectories with a learned recovery critic, achieving zero collisions in trials.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: Safety-critical high-speed legged locomotion requires motion planners to balance safety foresight with online computational efficiency. Although short prediction horizons reduce rollout costs, they provide limited safety foresight, and strict safety constraints severely restrict the feasible trajectory space. We propose a recovery-guided model-based diffusion (MBD) framework for safety-critical legged locomotion. It incorporates a learned terminal recovery critic into short-horizon trajectory optimization. Specifically, the critic approximates the worst-case future clearance margin along rollouts of a designated recovery policy. We introduce a feasibility-guided refinement strategy that combines within-horizon constraints and terminal recoverability at each sampling stage, while retaining feasible elites to mitigate sampling-support loss. Across 50 paired randomized Unitree Go2 obstacle-avoidance trials, our approach achieves zero collisions and 98% strict-clearance success, while requiring substantially less computation than long-horizon MBD baselines. A project page is available at https://zack4417.github.io/rg-mbd/.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Chenghao Gao, Zhi Zhang, Dian Jin, Yihe Pan, Doudou Zhou
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: WM-PPO enhances reinforcement learning by integrating a world model with a policy and critic to better predict and value future states, improving success rates significantly.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: A sparse terminal reward tells an agent little about its steps. Much of the missing information is implicit in the environment's dynamics, because each state transition can change the conditions for success long before the reward arrives. A world model trained on real transitions can learn to predict what each action changes, but a predicted observation does not by itself show whether success has become more likely. With a binary terminal reward, PPO's critic makes this judgment by estimating the current policy's probability of success, but only for states the agent reaches. Our method, WM-PPO, elegantly brings the two together. For each action the policy samples, executed or not, the world model predicts the next observation and the critic values the predicted successor. In the policy channel, comparisons among these values give the policy auxiliary advantages; in the value channel, their mean gives the critic an auxiliary target. A shared gate weights both channels according to how reliably comparisons with similar margins predicted real outcomes earlier in training. The policy, critic and world model all learn from the agent's own interaction, with no teacher or privileged information, and only the policy is used at inference. With a comparable number of real environment steps, WM-PPO raises success from PPO's 63.5% to 87.5% on ALFWorld and from 39.3% to 52.9% on ScienceWorld. It matches the strongest PPO refinements we tested on ALFWorld and exceeds the best of them by 6.5 points on ScienceWorld. The trained policy more often completes prerequisite steps before placing an object or committing to an answer.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Ke Sun, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Yike Zhang, Yanzhe Chen, Mike Zheng Shou
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: ForceHarness enables frozen multimodal models to effectively utilize force in robotic manipulation tasks by integrating self-regulating force primitives and a physics translation layer, significantly improving performance.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: Frontier multimodal models can now control robots zero-shot from images, yet many manipulation tasks depend on contact forces that images cannot show. Bringing force to an API-only frozen model raises two challenges. First, contact evolves much faster than an API model can decide, so the system must close the loop on force beneath the model. Second, a frozen model cannot interpret raw force streams, so force must be returned in a form the model can reason about. Therefore, we present ForceHarness, a harness that lets frozen models use force without demonstrations or finetuning. After calibrating hand force from a wrist sensor or joint torques alone, ForceHarness addresses the first challenge with self-terminating force primitives that regulate force on their own and return at a contact event. To address the second challenge, a physics translation layer turns each force trace into physical quantities with uncertainty as the tool result. To evaluate ForceHarness against expert force controllers and learned policies under identical conditions, we also build HiddenPhys, a seven-task MuJoCo benchmark with hidden physical variables. On a real arm without a wrist force sensor, ForceHarness raises the zero-shot success rate of GPT-6 Astra from 3.3% to 90.0%. In simulation, it adds 17.5 percentage points on the public ForceBench suite and 34.3 percentage points on HiddenPhys, surpassing force-aware policies trained on demonstrations on both benchmarks and matching hand-written expert controllers on HiddenPhys. Ablations further show that smaller models make significantly better decisions when given physical quantities rather than raw force values.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: ReAccess: Look Once, Stay Focused with Efficient Test Time Memory
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Tianhao Chen, Yilong Fan, Yuheng Wu, Xiaobin Hu, Dongman Lee
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: ReAccess introduces a lightweight framework for efficient visual grounding in vision-language models by utilizing compact associative memory for progressive evidence retrieval, enhancing performance and reducing computational overhead.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: Despite recent advances, vision-language models (VLMs) still struggle with fine-grained visual understanding, often failing to effectively utilize critical evidence already encoded in their visual representations. Existing approaches address this limitation through repeated visual processing or explicit reasoning, introducing substantial computational overhead. In this paper, we propose ReAccess, a lightweight framework that preserves and reuses question-relevant visual evidence through compact associative memory. Constructed during a single visual prefill, the memory supports progressive evidence retrieval that steers both attention queries and hidden representations, enabling effective visual grounding without repeated image encoding or explicit reasoning traces. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in both general visual understanding and fine-grained perception, while achieving substantially faster inference than existing reasoning-intensive approaches, demonstrating a promising path to efficient multimodal reasoning.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: Non-Imaging Optical Tactile Sensors for Robotics: Transduction Principles, System Integration, and Robotic Applications
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Hao Wu, Yu Feng, Haotian Guo, Huichan Zhao, Changsheng Wu
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: This review explores non-imaging optical tactile sensors in robotics, emphasizing their design, integration, and performance in accurately detecting contact variables amidst mechanical influences.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: Non-imaging optical tactile sensors encode contact through changes in optical intensity, wavelength, spectra, or photon counts, offering diverse architectures for robotic touch. Their usefulness depends on whether contact variables can be reliably distinguished from coupled mechanical and environmental effects, and whether the resulting information can be delivered in time to guide action. This review develops a unified framework linking mechanical load transmission, optical encoding, readout, and tactile inference to robotic task requirements. It examines reflective and waveguide-based devices, micro/nanofibers, fiber gratings, interferometric and resonant structures, and mechanoluminescent composites. Three considerations emerge across these approaches. First, high optical sensitivity supports accurate tactile estimation only when target variables remain identifiable under the relevant contact and calibration conditions. Second, spatial coverage and feedback timing must be assessed at the system level, accounting for multiplexing, acquisition, demodulation, and inference. Third, device characterization, offline recognition, and closed-loop robotic performance provide distinct levels of evidence and require different evaluation criteria. Representative studies illustrate how these considerations shape force estimation, contact localization, slip correction and distributed interaction. This review concludes with priorities for calibration transfer, reliable interfaces, scalable readout, and task-based validation, providing a basis for selecting and developing non-imaging optical tactile architectures for robotics.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: VLALagBench: Understanding When and Why VLA Inference Latency Matters
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Qi Wen, Borui Xu, Hussein Amro, Hongshi Tan, Hanmin Lin
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: VLALagBench is a benchmark revealing that VLA inference latency significantly impacts task success, particularly with moving targets, and offers predictive modeling for optimizing robot performance.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models offer a promising path toward general-purpose robot manipulation. While inference latency can affect task success in a constantly evolving physical world, the relationship between latency and task success rate remains poorly understood. In this paper, we introduce VLALagBench, a comprehensive benchmark for studying VLA inference latency sensitivity across task types, object speeds, execution modes (synchronous and asynchronous), and VLA policies. Using VLALagBench, we find that even a modest inference latency of 100 ms can nearly halve task success on moving targets, with sensitivity varying substantially across tasks and policies. These differences reflect task-specific requirements for precision and continuous motion. By overlapping inference with action execution, asynchronous execution can recover some of the lost success at the cost of more frequent inference requests. Building on these findings, we develop an empirical model that predicts task success from limited calibration data, achieving root-mean-square prediction errors of only 5.7-7.8% across various VLA policies. Given an inference system's latency and per-robot throughput, these predictions guide the selection of system-specific VLA algorithm configurations to maximize task success. We believe VLALagBench and these findings provide a solid foundation for future robotics algorithm-system co-design.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: Is Agentic AI Ready for Real-World Hardware Engineering? A Deep Dive with Phoenix-bench
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Qingyun Zou, Feng Yu, Hongshi Tan, Jiahao Cui, Bingsheng He
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: The paper evaluates agentic AI's effectiveness in hardware engineering using Phoenix-bench, revealing significant performance drops compared to software engineering due to inherent task differences and localization challenges.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: We ask whether agentic AI systems built for software engineering transfer to realistic hardware engineering. Existing hardware LLM benchmarks isolate sub-tasks but none jointly requires repository navigation, hierarchy-aware localization, Electronic Design Automation (EDA) executable verification, and maintenance-style patching. We introduce \textbf{Phoenix-bench}, a synchronized corpus of 511 verified Verilator instances from 114 GitHub repositories, each shipped with the developer patch, design-flow labels, fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass testbenches, and a Docker-pinned EDA environment so resolved-rate differences reflect agent behavior rather than toolchain availability. Using Phoenix-bench we run a uniform evaluation of four commercial agents and eight open-source agentic structures across four LLM backbones, plus two diagnostic interventions (file-level oracle localization and one round of testbench-log feedback). Three findings emerge. (i)~Software and hardware are fundamentally different engineering tasks: the same agent loses 37\% to 58\% from SWE-bench Verified to Phoenix-bench because hardware bugs propagate across parallel instantiated modules through signal flow rather than along a software-style call graph, and software-tuned agents stop at the symptom file instead of tracing back through the instantiation chain. (ii)~Failures concentrate on design control-flow / finite state machine (FSM) bugs, verification testbench bugs, and hard cases that demand cross-hierarchy signal-flow tracking and coordinated multi-file edits. (iii)~Localization granularity matters far more than localization itself: a perfect file-level oracle yields only $+1.4$\% because the agent then breaks files that did not need editing, while a single round of test case feedback lifts resolved rate by $42$\% to $45$\% because the test case tells \emph{where} the bug is and \emph{what} the fix has to look like.

Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.title: Stochastic Self-Distillation for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.authors_text: Jingru Guo, Alessandra Russo, Joey Bose, Christos Ziakas
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.summary: The VLA-SSD method enhances flow-based vision-language-action models by self-distilling a stochastic policy, improving efficiency and sample diversity while slightly reducing initial success rates.
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.debug_abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance in robotics through imitation learning, yet fine-tuning them with on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is limited. In group-based RL methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), every rollout step requires multi-step ODE integration, and the sampler's limited stochasticity leads to rollout groups with low variance. We propose VLA-SSD, which addresses both high inference latency and limited stochasticity. In particular, our method self-distills a pretrained flow-matching action head into a stochastic one-step policy by conditioning a single-jump generator on a Brownian path. We derive a conditional action density via our stochastic one-step policy, enabling efficient post-training via likelihood-ratio RL algorithms. We show that distilling VLA-SSD from the $π_0$ VLA reduces the action head's forward-pass time by a factor of 7.7, at the cost of a 5.5% relative decrease in the success rate on the LIBERO benchmark. However, by leveraging the increased sample diversity of VLA-SSD during group generation, post-training a $π_{0.5}$ VLA using GRPO yields a 20.6% relative improvement.

Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.title: CODE-SHARP: Continuous Open-ended Discovery and Evolution of Skills as Hierarchical Reward Programs
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.authors_text: Richard Bornemann, Pierluigi Vito Amadori, Antoine Cully
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.summary: CODE-SHARP autonomously evolves a hierarchy of skill-encoding programs, enabling agents to learn complex tasks efficiently without predefined rewards, outperforming existing methods significantly.
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.debug_abstract: A core quality of general intelligence is the ability to open-endedly expand and evolve its set of mastered skills autonomously. While recent Foundation Model (FM) driven approaches have shown promising results towards this goal, they typically rely on significant human-in-the-loop engineering, limiting their transferability to novel environments. To address this, we introduce Continuous Open-ended Discovery and Evolution of Skills as Hierarchical Reward Programs (CODE-SHARP), a framework that leverages FMs to open-endedly grow and evolve an archive of Python programs encoding skills to train a generalist agent policy entirely from scratch via reinforcement learning, directly from source code. These programs, termed Skills as Hierarchical Reward Programs (SHARPs), each encode a local success condition and a set of prerequisites delegated to previously discovered SHARPs. At runtime, SHARPs dynamically route the agent through their prerequisite chain based on the current state, rewarding each completion along the way, requiring the agent to learn only the marginal behaviour each new SHARP introduces, enabling efficient learning of long-horizon skills without any pre-defined rewards. On Craftax-Classic and XLand-MiniGrid, agents trained fully autonomously by CODE-SHARP outperform previous works by 6x and 2.7x in median performance and are the only agents capable of crafting iron tools and mining diamonds. On AI2-THOR, CODE-SHARP achieves 66.7% median success versus 0% for ELLM and OMNI, using only the initial environment state instead of the full source code. Scaled to Craftax-Extended, CODE-SHARP trains a generalist agent on over 90 discovered SHARPs, enabling the agent to solve challenging long-horizon tasks zero-shot, matching agents trained on ground-truth rewards.

Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.title: Successive Convexification in Learned World Models for Safe Offline Planning
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.summary: The paper presents a successive convex program for safe offline planning in learned world models, improving safety and performance over traditional sampling-based methods.
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.debug_abstract: World models learned from offline data allow an agent to plan without further interaction with the environment, but the sampling-based planners used with them handle safety constraints only by scoring or rejecting sampled action sequences. We instead pose safe planning in the latent space of a learned world model as a successive convex program (SCP), in which a learned discrete-time control barrier function is imposed as a constraint at every step of the horizon. SCP requires smooth dynamics, so we build the networks from smoothed MaxMin activations and spectrally normalised layers, and bound the resulting linearisation error in terms of the Lipschitz bound and the smoothing width. As SCP is a local method, we start it from a sampled plan. On two Safety-Gymnasium navigation tasks with offline data, this planner has fewer violations than MPPI and CEM drawing 128 times as many samples at equal wall-clock time in our main comparison, though not significantly, and earns greater return at longer horizons, and is much safer than SCP without a sampled start. SCP converged more often on Lipschitz-bounded models. Unlike sampling, it also reports at each step whether its plan is a feasible, first-order optimal KKT point of the planning problem in the model, or that no feasible plan was found nearby. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/youngers2006/scwm.

深圳大学.title: Bridging Semantic Logic Gaps: A Cognition Inspired Multimodal Boundary Preserving Network for Image Manipulation Localization
深圳大学.authors_text: Songlin Li, Zhiqing Guo, Yuanman Li, Zeyu Li, Yunfeng Diao
深圳大学.summary: The paper presents CMB-Net, a cognition-inspired multimodal network that enhances image manipulation localization by integrating semantic analysis from large language models and preserving boundary information.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: The existing image manipulation localization (IML) models mainly relies on visual cues, but ignores the semantic logical relationships between content features. In fact, the content semantics conveyed by real images often conform to human cognitive laws. However, image manipulation technology usually destroys the internal relationship between content features, thus leaving semantic clues for IML. In this paper, we propose a cognition inspired multimodal boundary preserving network (CMB-Net). Specifically, CMB-Net utilizes large language models (LLMs) to analyze manipulated regions within images and generate prompt-based textual information to compensate for the lack of semantic relationships in the visual information. Considering that the erroneous texts induced by hallucination from LLMs will damage the accuracy of IML, we propose an image-text central ambiguity module (ITCAM). It assigns weights to the text features by quantifying the ambiguity between text and image features, thereby ensuring the beneficial impact of textual information. We also propose an image-text interaction module (ITIM) that aligns visual and text features using a correlation matrix for fine-grained interaction. Finally, inspired by invertible neural networks, we propose a restoration edge decoder (RED) that mutually generates input and output features to preserve boundary information in manipulated regions without loss. Extensive experiments show that CMB-Net outperforms most existing IML models. Our code is available on https://github.com/vpsg-research/CMB-Net.

深圳大学.title: Navi-Agent: Unlocalized Monocular Navigation Agent
深圳大学.authors_text: Wenyuan Xie, Mengyang Hong, Yongzhong Wang, Yanbiao Ji, Yijin Zhou
深圳大学.summary: Navi-Agent is a zero-shot VLN-CE system that utilizes a coordinate-free spatial state from visual observations for effective navigation and task verification in unknown environments.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires an embodied agent to execute long-horizon instructions in unknown environments. Existing zero-shot VLN-CE systems typically maintain spatial states through geometric localization or coordinate-based representations. Recent geometry-constrained navigation removes depth and globally consistent coordinates, but maintaining persistent spatial awareness for place confirmation, progress verification, and recovery remains challenging. We present Navi-Agent, a zero-shot VLN-CE agent that constructs a coordinate-free spatial state from visual observations and executed motion histories. Navi-Agent organizes this state as a navigation topology, where nodes represent visual places and edges represent motion transitions. This representation enables observation-based approximate self-localization, task progress verification, and visual revisitation-based recovery. Navi-Agent performs closed-loop navigation by decomposing instructions into sub-goals, executing local visual navigation, and verifying visited places through the constructed spatial state. Experiments on zero-shot VLN-CE benchmark and real-world robot platforms show that Navi-Agent achieves state-of-the-art performance among geometry-constrained methods while remaining competitive with approaches relying on geometric localization.

深圳大学.title: AffectAgent: Collaborative Multi-Agent Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Emotion Recognition
深圳大学.authors_text: Zeheng Wang, Zitong Yu, Yijie Zhu, Bo Zhao, Haochen Liang
深圳大学.summary: AffectAgent is a collaborative multi-agent framework that enhances multimodal emotion recognition by optimizing retrieval and decision-making to better capture complex affective states.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: LLM-based multimodal emotion recognition relies on static parametric memory and often hallucinates when interpreting nuanced affective states. In this paper, given that single-round retrieval-augmented generation is highly susceptible to modal ambiguity and therefore struggles to capture complex affective dependencies across modalities, we introduce AffectAgent, an affect-oriented multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation framework that leverages collaborative decision-making among agents for fine-grained affective understanding. Specifically, AffectAgent comprises three jointly optimized specialized agents, namely a query planner, an evidence filter, and an emotion generator, which collaboratively perform analytical reasoning to retrieve cross-modal samples, assess evidence, and generate predictions. These agents are optimized end-to-end using Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) with a shared affective reward to ensure consistent emotion understanding. Furthermore, we introduce Modality-Balancing Mixture of Experts (MB-MoE) and Retrieval-Augmented Adaptive Fusion (RAAF), where MB-MoE dynamically regulates the contributions of different modalities to mitigate representation mismatch caused by cross-modal heterogeneity, while RAAF enhances semantic completion under missing-modality conditions by incorporating retrieved audiovisual embeddings. Extensive experiments on MER-UniBench demonstrate that AffectAgent achieves superior performance across complex scenarios. Our code will be released at: https://github.com/Wz1h1NG1/AffectAgent.

深圳大学.title: SGR3 Model: Scene Graph Retrieval-Reasoning Model in 3D
深圳大学.authors_text: Zirui Wang, Ruiping Liu, Yufan Chen, Junwei Zheng, Weijia Fan
深圳大学.summary: The SGR3 Model introduces a training-free framework for 3D scene graph generation using multi-modal large language models and retrieval-augmented generation, enhancing relational reasoning without explicit reconstruction.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: 3D scene graphs provide a structured representation of object entities and their relationships, enabling high-level interpretation and reasoning for robots while remaining intuitively understandable to humans. Existing approaches for 3D scene graph generation typically combine scene reconstruction with graph neural networks (GNNs). However, such pipelines require multi-modal data that may not always be available, and their reliance on heuristic graph construction can constrain the prediction of relationship triplets. In this work, we introduce a Scene Graph Retrieval-Reasoning Model in 3D (SGR3 Model), a training-free framework that leverages multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for semantic scene graph generation. SGR3 Model bypasses the need for explicit 3D reconstruction. Instead, it enhances relational reasoning by incorporating semantically aligned scene graphs retrieved via a ColPali-style cross-modal framework. To improve retrieval robustness, we further introduce a weighted patch-level similarity selection mechanism that mitigates the negative impact of blurry or semantically uninformative regions. Experiments demonstrate that SGR3 Model achieves competitive performance compared to training-free baselines and on par with GNN-based expert models. Moreover, an ablation study on the retrieval module and knowledge base scale reveals that retrieved external information is explicitly integrated into the token generation process, rather than being implicitly internalized through abstraction.

深圳大学.title: Remember, Replay, Adapt: Learning from Past Experience in Online Vision-and-Language Navigation
深圳大学.authors_text: Chenhao Ding, Jizhou Han, Lixin Xiu, Muyao Wang, Songlin Dong
深圳大学.summary: The R2A framework enhances online vision-and-language navigation by leveraging past experiences through Success-Failure Memory and Prior-Anchored Adaptation for improved policy learning and performance.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: Existing feedback-based methods for online vision-and-language navigation (VLN) primarily learn from current episode outcomes, leaving previously acquired feedback underutilized. Inspired by human episodic memory, we propose R2A, an online VLN adaptation framework that continually reuses successful and failed navigation experiences for policy learning. Specifically, Success-Failure Memory (SFM) retains successful and failed navigation episodes with acquired feedback and retrieves task-relevant experiences based on incoming instructions, enabling historical feedback to guide subsequent navigation. Prior-Anchored Adaptation (PAA) learns from these experiences by reinforcing successful trajectories and suppressing failed ones relative to a frozen pretrained policy, while regularizing behavioral drift. Together, these modules enable continual feedback reuse and stable policy adaptation without source-domain data or expert supervision. Extensive experiments across three benchmarks, REVERIE, R2R, and R2R-CE, and five navigation backbones demonstrate consistent performance gains. On the REVERIE validation unseen split, R2A improves DUET's SR from 46.98% to 69.84% and SPL from 33.73% to 50.98%.

深圳大学.title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
深圳大学.authors_text: Jiajun Sun, Zeyu Zhang, Zeyu Ren, Guangfeng Jiang, Yang Zhao
深圳大学.summary: PanDWM introduces a panoramic 4D driving world model that enhances video generation efficiency and consistency by integrating multiple camera views into a continuous 360° image.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one $360^\circ$ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched $360^\circ$ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at $8$-$46\times$ their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.

四川大学.title: CivilBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Information Integration in Civil Engineering
四川大学.authors_text: Dan Yuan, Yue Wen, Zhili He, Zhenkui Zhou, Shicen Liu
四川大学.summary: CivilBench is a new benchmark for assessing vision-language models in civil engineering, highlighting significant reasoning limitations and offering a framework for improving AI-assisted decision-making.
四川大学.debug_abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), is increasingly applied in civil and structural engineering for disaster assessment, structural analysis, and engineering decision support. However, the extent to which current VLMs possess the reasoning capabilities required for reliable engineering judgments remains unclear. In this work, we introduce CivilBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs in civil engineering and disaster-related scenarios. CivilBench covers three major task families: Sequential Reasoning, Image-based Structural Understanding, and Open-world Understanding, encompassing numerical reasoning, structural damage assessment, risk inference, causal analysis, and repair planning. The benchmark is constructed through a systematic pipeline of domain-specific data collection, engineering-oriented captioning, expert annotation, question design, and quality verification. Evaluation of representative state-of-the-art VLMs reveals substantial limitations in domain-specific reasoning, with Sequential Reasoning emerging as a major bottleneck, particularly when models must infer numerical relationships from sparse structured observations. Further experiments show that numerical priors and external knowledge can alleviate these limitations, although their effectiveness depends on the model's ability to reliably interpret and use the available evidence. CivilBench provides a capability-oriented testbed for identifying reasoning limitations and evaluating progress toward reliable AI-assisted engineering decision-making. The benchmark will be publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/traceuryuan/CivilBench.

四川大学.title: UNITE: Consolidating Embodied VLM Specialists via Shared-Anchor One-Bit Factorization
四川大学.authors_text: Tao Tao, Anke Tang, Enneng Yang, Zhi Hou, Xiaogang Wang
四川大学.summary: UNITE consolidates multiple embodied vision-language specialists into a compact model using shared-anchor one-bit factorization, maintaining performance while significantly reducing storage requirements.
四川大学.debug_abstract: Embodied capabilities such as visual grounding, spatial reasoning, navigation, and driving understanding are often developed in separate vision-language specialists fine-tuned from a common pretrained model.Deploying the specialists separately multiplies storage, whereas merging them into one dense model forces conflicting task updates to share parameters and loses part of each specialist's expertise.We introduce UNITE, a framework that consolidates such specialists into a compact shared-backbone mixture of experts. UNITE keeps the feed-forward block of each specialist as a routable expert and represents the expert bank through a shared-anchor one-bit factorization: a shared floating-point anchor plus expert-specific, row-scaled binary deviations.The anchor is optimized jointly with the scales and signs through closed-form alternating updates, using only source weights and no calibration data.Router adaptation then adjusts token-level expert selection with the backbone and experts frozen, updating fewer than $0.6$M parameters ($<0.01\%$ of the $8.8$B active parameters). Built from four Qwen3-VL-8B specialists, the complete UNITE model occupies $20.3$ GB, $1.16\times$ the storage of one dense specialist and $59.6\%$ below the uncompressed MoE. Across $22$ benchmarks and R2R Val-Unseen, UNITE matches six static merging methods in mean retention of best-specialist performance, leads all of them on Scan2Cap, ScanQA, and all four navigation metrics, and surpasses every source specialist on all five 3D scene understanding benchmarks (up to $+19.1$ on Scan2Cap) and on R2R navigation. Relative to the uncompressed MoE, factorization is nearly lossless on $21$ of $22$ benchmarks; the exception is VSI-Bench, where frame-count experiments suggest impaired use of cross-frame evidence.UNITE thus consolidates complementary embodied capabilities near single-model storage.

四川大学.title: GEM-MM: Reducing VLM Hallucination with Entropy-Guided Preference Alignment
四川大学.summary: GEM-MM enhances vision-language models by employing entropy-guided preference alignment, significantly reducing hallucination rates while improving accuracy and preference scores under limited data conditions.
四川大学.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are routinely aligned with offline pairwise RLHF objectives, but multimodal preference data is scarce and treats every response token as equally informative. Under a small preference budget, pair construction becomes nearly irrelevant: standard DPO-style, image-conditional, and self-improvement objectives all perform within 1.1 points on MM-RLHF metrics and 0.5 points on hallucination rates, matching the SFT baseline. We call this entropy-blind preference optimization: the learning signal ignores policy uncertainty, which in chain-of-thought VLMs concentrates on specific fork tokens where visual claims are made. We introduce GEM-MM, extending entropy-guided preference modeling to VLMs. It samples on-policy candidates, rewards high-entropy reasoning forks, penalizes uncertain final answers, and updates the model via group-normalized policy gradients. On a 3000-prompt MM-RLHF budget with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, GEM-MM achieves the best entropy-depth preference score (61.7% vs. 57.3-58.4% baselines) and implicit-reward accuracy (41.4%). Crucially, it reduces AMBER hallucination from 23.4-24.0 to 20.6 and CHAIR from 5.0-5.1 to 4.6 at matched caption coverage. It also ranks best on all three HallusionBench granularities, with a conservative operating point raising the near-chosen rate to 62.4%. An off-the-shelf multimodal reward model ranks GEM-MM first, and two such models independently confirm our main ablations (p < 0.001). We report confidence intervals, paired significance tests, metric-reward functional overlaps, and document a collapse mode when exceeding the fair budget. Code and evaluation harness: https://github.com/SNOWTEAM2023/GEM-MM

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Difference-in-Differences on a Censored Rating Scale Can Manufacture an Effect: Evidence from a Pre-Registered LLM-Judge Audit
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Shuyi Fan, Boyuan Deng, Mengyu Xu, Xinhong Xie, Chenyang Li
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The study reveals that a severity shift in ratings can falsely indicate bias in LLM-judge audits, as shown through a pre-registered analysis of response preferences.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: LLM-judge audits assess bias by comparing ratings across matched conditions. Difference-in-differences designs take the rating difference between two candidate responses to each item and compare it across a manipulated attribute. Building on prior work on nonlinear difference-in-differences, we show in closed form that when ratings are bounded, a severity shift common to both responses produces an observed interaction whenever the scale bounds attenuate it unequally. We then report a pre-registered audit of 990 calls to a frozen pedagogy judge. The registered primary analysis did not detect an effect of a stated novice or advanced profile on the judge's preference for a high-scaffolding over a low-scaffolding response. The only nominally significant secondary interaction was on the productive-struggle sub-score ($+0.378$ points, $p = 0.002$). A post-hoc construction in which the profile shifts both responses' latent ratings equally reproduced 79 to 85% of this interaction using the observed severity shift and the scale floor alone. The observed interaction therefore does not identify differential preference on the latent scale.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Data-Driven Exploration for a Class of Continuous-Time Indefinite Linear--Quadratic Reinforcement Learning Problems
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: This paper presents a model-free, adaptive exploration method for continuous-time indefinite linear-quadratic reinforcement learning, enhancing efficiency and convergence while achieving optimal regret bounds.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: We study reinforcement learning (RL) for a class of continuous-time stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) control problems, where volatilities depend on both states and controls while states are scalar-valued and there are no running control rewards, the last feature also leading to the so-called indefinite LQ controls. We propose a model-free, data-driven exploration mechanism that adaptively adjusts entropy regularization by the critic and policy variance by the actor. Unlike the constant or deterministic exploration schedules employed in the existing literature, which require extensive tuning for implementations and ignore learning progress during iterations, our adaptive exploratory approach boosts learning efficiency with minimal tuning. Despite its flexibility, our method achieves a sublinear regret bound that matches the best-known model-free results for this class of LQ problems, which were previously derived only with fixed exploration schedules. Numerical experiments demonstrate that adaptive explorations accelerate convergence and improve regret performance compared to the non-adaptive model-free and model-based counterparts.

高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).title: SGR3 Model: Scene Graph Retrieval-Reasoning Model in 3D
高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).authors_text: Zirui Wang, Ruiping Liu, Yufan Chen, Junwei Zheng, Weijia Fan
高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).summary: The SGR3 Model introduces a training-free framework for 3D scene graph generation using multi-modal large language models and retrieval-augmented generation, enhancing relational reasoning without explicit reconstruction.
高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).debug_abstract: 3D scene graphs provide a structured representation of object entities and their relationships, enabling high-level interpretation and reasoning for robots while remaining intuitively understandable to humans. Existing approaches for 3D scene graph generation typically combine scene reconstruction with graph neural networks (GNNs). However, such pipelines require multi-modal data that may not always be available, and their reliance on heuristic graph construction can constrain the prediction of relationship triplets. In this work, we introduce a Scene Graph Retrieval-Reasoning Model in 3D (SGR3 Model), a training-free framework that leverages multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for semantic scene graph generation. SGR3 Model bypasses the need for explicit 3D reconstruction. Instead, it enhances relational reasoning by incorporating semantically aligned scene graphs retrieved via a ColPali-style cross-modal framework. To improve retrieval robustness, we further introduce a weighted patch-level similarity selection mechanism that mitigates the negative impact of blurry or semantically uninformative regions. Experiments demonstrate that SGR3 Model achieves competitive performance compared to training-free baselines and on par with GNN-based expert models. Moreover, an ablation study on the retrieval module and knowledge base scale reveals that retrieved external information is explicitly integrated into the token generation process, rather than being implicitly internalized through abstraction.

通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).title: NF-VLA: A Normalizing-Flow Baseline for Vision-Language-Action Learning
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).authors_text: Ruichen Deng, Qinyu Zhao, Yong-Hyun Park, Mutian Tong, Liang Zheng
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).summary: NF-VLA introduces a competitive vision-language-action learning framework using autoregressive normalizing flows for efficient training and refinement of robot action policies.
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).debug_abstract: Autoregressive normalizing flows (NFs) provide a tractable density for learning and sampling continuous robot actions. We show that a single maximum-likelihood objective can train vision--language--action (VLA) policies competitive with leading methods on manipulation benchmarks. We present NF-VLA, which combines conditional autoregressive normalizing flows with score-based action refinement. Its deep--shallow architecture concentrates visual, language, and proprioceptive prefix conditioning in a high-capacity deep block, while unconditioned shallow blocks provide a shared invertible action transformation. The vision--language backbone and flow are jointly trained by exact maximum likelihood on Gaussian-smoothed action chunks. The same learned density supplies a single score-based correction at inference, refining generated actions to account for training-time smoothing without a separately trained denoiser. Trained on LIBERO from a pretrained vision--language backbone without robot pretraining, NF-VLA achieves 98.35\% success across the four standard suites and 72.6\% on LIBERO-Plus using the same checkpoint without further fine-tuning. Ablations show that deep-only prefix conditioning and score-based refinement both improve closed-loop success. Together, these results establish carefully structured autoregressive flows as a competitive approach to VLA control, with one learned density supporting policy training, action generation, and refinement.

Quest for Intelligence.title: Multi-CONDOR: Learning Multistable Motion Primitives from Demonstration
Quest for Intelligence.authors_text: Gabriele Giuseppe Di Marzo, Mariano Ramírez Montero, Maximilian Stölzle, Rodrigo Pérez-Dattari, Cosimo Della Santina
Quest for Intelligence.summary: The multi-CONDOR framework learns versatile motion primitives for robots, enabling convergence to multiple discrete or continuous goals while enhancing stability and performance in manipulation tasks.
Quest for Intelligence.debug_abstract: Dynamical-system-based motion policies provide a framework for learning reactive robot motions with stability and convergence properties. Many manipulation tasks, however, admit several distinct goals or a continuous set of acceptable outcomes, requiring motion primitives that preserve these alternatives. Accommodating both goal structures within a unified framework with continuous, autonomous dynamics remains an open challenge. We propose a CONDOR-based framework, multi-CONDOR, for learning motion primitives with either multiple discrete attractors or a continuous attracting goal contour. The approach combines imitation learning with losses that encourage agreement between the learned task dynamics and latent reference systems encoding the desired attraction structure. We provide a Lyapunov-based analysis of the convergence properties of the learned motion dynamics. We evaluate the framework on simulated benchmarks with discrete goals, qualitative examples with continuous goal contours, and robotic grasping experiments. In simulation, multi-CONDOR reduces trajectory RMSE by approximately 72% compared with separately learned single-goal motion primitives selected by a state machine. For tasks with two and three goals, respectively, it reduces the fraction of evaluated initial states ending outside the goal tolerance from StableNODE's 0.31% and 7.29% to 0% in both settings. Experiments with a Franka Emika robot arm demonstrate successful grasping of a container by either of its two handles using motions learned from demonstrations. Together, these results show multi-CONDOR combines motion reproduction with the flexibility to converge to alternative valid outcomes.

Quest for Intelligence.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
Quest for Intelligence.authors_text: Yuhan Tang, Ke Fan, Xinkai Zou, Baichuan Mo, Kangxin Cui
Quest for Intelligence.summary: The paper introduces Ask2Decide, a benchmark assessing LLM agents' ability to acquire crucial decision-relevant information from humans, revealing significant challenges in planning accuracy.
Quest for Intelligence.debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

Quest for Intelligence.title: WarpMPC: Large-Batch MPC on GPU via ADMM with Unrolled $LDL^\top$ Factorization
Quest for Intelligence.authors_text: Henrik Hose, Se Hwan Jeon, Charles Khazoom, Sangbae Kim, Sebastian Trimpe
Quest for Intelligence.summary: The paper presents WarpMPC, a GPU-optimized toolbox for efficient large-batch model-predictive control, achieving significant throughput improvements in solving sequential quadratic programming iterations.
Quest for Intelligence.debug_abstract: This paper introduces numerical optimizations for maximizing throughput on GPU when solving large batches (10,000 to over 100,000) of sequential quadratic programming (SQP) iterations, where all problems have the same structure. The optimizations are implemented in a toolbox WarpMPC for model-predictive control (MPC) in JAX and Warp. Based on the insight that all MPC problem instances in a batch share the same sparsity in time, cost, and constraints, we propose unrolling sparse linear factorizations and solves, which dominate alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) solver runtime. We avoid memory access bottlenecks and wasting computations via optimized memory layout, padding-reducing segmentation of the unrolled factorization, and dependency level scheduled backsolves, additionally accelerating sensitivity computation. We achieve throughputs of 8,000 to 250,000 SQP iterations per second on nonlinear cartpole, quadrotor, and humanoid robot benchmarks, outperforming baselines by 3$\times$ to 25$\times$. We illustrate practical usefulness by synthesizing a dataset and training a neural network approximation of an MPC in under 5 minutes that stabilizes a nano quadrotor in hardware experiments.

Quest for Intelligence.title: Illumination-Robust Localization around Unknown Space Objects using Multispectral Image Fusion
Quest for Intelligence.authors_text: Eric J. Elias, Michael Esswein, Jonathan P. How, David W. Miller
Quest for Intelligence.summary: This paper presents a multispectral image fusion approach combining visible and thermal-infrared data to enhance localization and mapping around unknown space objects under varying lighting conditions.
Quest for Intelligence.debug_abstract: As on-orbit operations grow, so does the need for precise navigation around unknown resident space objects (RSOs), such as spacecraft, debris, and asteroids. Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithms are often studied for mapping an RSO and estimating the inspector's relative pose, but conventional cameras struggle during eclipse, while lidar, though illumination-robust, has higher SWaP. Thermal-infrared cameras track targets through difficult lighting but lack the resolution and feature-richness of visible cameras. Images of a target satellite in low Earth orbit are simulated in both visible and thermal bands, and fused at the pixel level to combine each sensor's strengths for front-end tracking. Thermal imagery is further exploited by a novel silhouette-based visual place recognition (VPR) method that detects loop closures without training, runs entirely on CPU, and outperforms all baselines. Integrated SLAM performance is compared using visible, thermal-infrared, and fused imagery across lighting conditions, trajectories, and place recognition methods; using fused imagery for front-end tracking and our thermal-silhouette place recognition method performs best. The results show that visible and thermal modalities each provide unique information that is exploited differently at various stages of navigation. These low-SWaP sensors could ultimately enable reliable proximity operations on smaller, lower-cost spacecraft.

天津大学.title: ReAccess: Look Once, Stay Focused with Efficient Test Time Memory
天津大学.authors_text: Tianhao Chen, Yilong Fan, Yuheng Wu, Xiaobin Hu, Dongman Lee
天津大学.summary: ReAccess introduces a lightweight framework for efficient visual grounding in vision-language models by utilizing compact associative memory for progressive evidence retrieval, enhancing performance and reducing computational overhead.
天津大学.debug_abstract: Despite recent advances, vision-language models (VLMs) still struggle with fine-grained visual understanding, often failing to effectively utilize critical evidence already encoded in their visual representations. Existing approaches address this limitation through repeated visual processing or explicit reasoning, introducing substantial computational overhead. In this paper, we propose ReAccess, a lightweight framework that preserves and reuses question-relevant visual evidence through compact associative memory. Constructed during a single visual prefill, the memory supports progressive evidence retrieval that steers both attention queries and hidden representations, enabling effective visual grounding without repeated image encoding or explicit reasoning traces. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in both general visual understanding and fine-grained perception, while achieving substantially faster inference than existing reasoning-intensive approaches, demonstrating a promising path to efficient multimodal reasoning.

人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).title: GameReplica: A Benchmark for Black-Box Visual Game Replication by Vision-Language Agents
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).authors_text: Boyu Qiao, Zixin Tang, Kaige Li, Xiaoshuai Hao, Dongyu She
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).summary: GameReplica introduces a benchmark for assessing vision-language agents' ability to replicate black-box web games, revealing significant challenges in rule consistency versus visual fidelity across various models.
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).debug_abstract: Benchmarks for coding agents typically assess implementation from explicit specifications, leaving open whether agents can discover and reproduce systems whose rules are undocumented and accessible only through interaction. We study this capability in web games, which offer controlled environments with observable actions and outcomes, and introduce GameReplica, a benchmark for end-to-end black-box game replication. It comprises 125 instances spanning 25 web games and five core mechanism families, with each game instantiated at five difficulty levels. Under container isolation, an agent accesses the target game only through an action--screenshot interface, may iterate between probing the game, implementing a replica, and checking it, and delivers a self-contained runnable replica together with a rule checklist. A reference-grounded evaluation then scores the deliverables separately on rule consistency, implementation consistency, and visual fidelity. Experiments across six models and five agent runtimes show that black-box replication remains challenging: Claude Opus 4.8 achieves the highest Overall score, 71.6%, while the other models obtain 4.0%--43.0%. Every model scores highest on visual fidelity and lowest on rule consistency, suggesting that reproducing appearance is easier than recovering mechanics. Difficulty widens the gap: from L1 to L5, the four lower-scoring models show relative Overall score declines of 33%--63%, whereas the strongest model declines by less than 5%. In the evaluated configurations, outcomes vary more across models than across agent runtimes, and most attributed failures of weaker models arise during exploration, before replica code is written. Resources and interactive demonstrations are available at https://qqqqqqby.github.io/GameReplica/.

人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).title: AITHER: Authority-Informed Evidence Routing for Mixed-Authority Vision-Language Reasoning
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).authors_text: Xinjin Li, Haoyue Zhang, Xinyi Gou, Yuruo Gong, Yuanjian He
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).summary: AITHER introduces a novel framework for mixed-authority vision-language reasoning, achieving high accuracy by effectively routing evidence based on authority, improving claim correction while preserving task integrity.
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).debug_abstract: Reliable vision-language reasoning requires a control decision that conventional grounding methods leave implicit: which input is entitled to determine the answer? Auxiliary text may be a defeasible claim about an image, a binding task instruction, or compatible context. Correcting every image-text conflict toward the image therefore repairs false claims but overwrites valid task rules. We formalize this setting as mixed-authority vision-language reasoning and introduce AITHER, an Authority-Informed Text-Image Hierarchy for Evidence Routing. Its final policy, the Semantic-Frame Router, is a training-free black-box control layer that (i) compiles explicit task directives, (ii) recovers standardized spatial frames from metadata-scrubbed pixels, (iii) resolves the semantic polarity of remaining notes, and (iv) routes among frozen observable candidates with fail-closed semantics. This ordered decomposition converts authority arbitration from an unconstrained prompt preference into a reproducible inference program. Across 1,620 MATRIX predictions, AITHER reaches 95.1% accuracy, exceeding the strongest task-and-frame baseline by 9.1 points with a 95% record-cluster interval of 6.8-11.5 points and no harmed records. It further reaches 100.0% on 1,800 controlled FRAME predictions and 93.3% on GQA-MATRIX. The results show that explicit authority routing can simultaneously improve false-claim correction, preserve task-defined answers, and eliminate clean-context overcorrection.

人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).title: MetricHand: Geometry-Aware Flow Matching for 4D Hand Reconstruction in Metric World Space
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).authors_text: Yibo Bai, Likui Zhang, Jinglei Zhang, Zhengbin Pang, Xingshen Song
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).summary: MetricHand introduces a geometry-aware flow matching framework for accurate 4D hand reconstruction in metric space, significantly enhancing localization and temporal fidelity under occlusion.
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).debug_abstract: Egocentric hand motion provides physical motion supervision for dexterous manipulation and vision-language-action pretraining. Reliable use of this supervision requires accurate and temporally coherent 4D hand reconstruction in metric world space. Existing methods typically lift framewise estimates produced under weak perspective into world coordinates. By ignoring joint-dependent depth variation at close range, this approximation couples errors in translation, orientation, and articulation that persist after world lifting and worsen under occlusion. We present MetricHand, a geometry-aware flow matching framework for 4D hand reconstruction in metric world space. MetricHand encodes depth priors from hand-object interaction regions into joint-associated representations that preserve local spatial structure and metric scale. Fused with visual features, this geometry guides coarse metric estimation and conditions every step of temporal generation. The model jointly recovers world-space translation, global orientation, MANO articulation, and shape, while structural priors and temporal context support estimation under partial occlusion. MetricHand reduces camera-space MPJPE by 49.3% and 52.9%, absolute world-space MPJPE by 28.7% and 21.7%, and wrist localization error by 48.5% and 37.9% relative to HaWoR, respectively. World-space acceleration error decreases by 44.2% and 64.3%, demonstrating improved temporal fidelity alongside more accurate absolute localization.

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).title: Polygraph: Large-Scale Multi-Session Trajectory Optimization using Pose Graphs
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Petar Lukovic, Tian Yi Lim, Marc Pollefeys, Pablo Speciale, Hermann Blum
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).summary: Polygraph introduces an online multi-session trajectory optimization method that efficiently integrates independent trajectories into a globally consistent pose graph without building a 3D map.
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: Robots, vehicles, and wearable devices often traverse the same environment many times. Each pass produces its own trajectory from onboard visual or visual-inertial odometry. These trajectories are locally accurate but drift over time and live in unrelated coordinate frames. Turning many such independent trajectories into one globally consistent set is the large-scale multi-session trajectory optimization problem. Existing solutions largely work offline. All sessions must be available up front, one session is fixed as the reference frame, and a single fused map is then optimized. This paper presents Polygraph, a multi-session trajectory optimization pipeline that processes sessions online, one keyframe and one spatial cluster at a time, and never builds a 3D map. Keyframes are grouped into local clusters. When a cluster closes, it is matched against every other session through learned image retrieval. Candidate pairs are verified with sparse feature matching, monocular metric depth, and robust pose estimation. A two-tier consensus gate admits a cross-session edge into the shared pose graph only once independent evidence corroborates it. A cheap incremental solve keeps the graph current, and a periodic robust batch solve prunes outliers. We evaluate Polygraph on stereo outdoor driving, HoloLens and iPad indoor traversals, legged indoor locomotion with a Boston Dynamics Spot, and large-scale outdoor vehicle and handheld routes. Against the closest prior work on the same GPU model, using its reported timings, Polygraph runs faster, commits fewer loop-closure edges, and matches or improves on accuracy.

上海科技大学.title: TaF-Foundation: Wrench-Grounded Cross-Sensor Tactile Representations
上海科技大学.authors_text: Jiaming Jiang, Yuzhe Huang, Baokun Yang, Hao Liang, Li Gao
上海科技大学.summary: The TaF-Foundation framework enables cross-sensor tactile representation learning by grounding observations in wrenches, improving manipulation and sensor adaptability through a shared feature space.
上海科技大学.debug_abstract: Tactile sensing is essential for contact-rich manipulation, yet heterogeneous sensing mechanisms and observation formats hinder cross-hardware transfer. Since physical contact is governed by Newtonian mechanics, we ground tactile representations in six-dimensional wrenches, establishing a common physical reference across sensing mechanisms. Specifically, we pair tactile observations from all sensors with wrench measurements, enabling shared physical supervision without requiring direct tactile-to-tactile pairing between sensors. To support learning at scale, we develop a dedicated acquisition platform and collect over 100 million paired tactile observations and wrench measurements from 24 sensors spanning four families of sensing principles. Building on this dataset, our framework combines sensor-specific input adaptation with a shared tactile encoder. By learning to reconstruct wrenches, the encoder maps observations from different sensors into a shared, continuous feature space grounded in contact physics. To leverage these representations for manipulation, we introduce TaF-Policy, which integrates tactile features with visual observations and robot states to generate action chunks. We evaluate the learned representations through wrench estimation, cross-sensor retrieval, few-shot adaptation to unseen sensors, and robotic manipulation. On the core benchmark, our method reduces single-frame force RMSE by 17.1% and improves cross-sensor retrieval R@1 by 13.11 percentage points over the strongest baseline. In manipulation experiments, TaF-Policy achieves average success rates of 51.33% across three simulated tasks and 46.25% across four real-world tasks, compared with 47.33% and 23.75%, respectively, for the strongest baselines evaluated on the same task sets. Project page: https://mrjiangjm.github.io/TaF-Foundation/.

上海科技大学.title: WiFi-based Global Localization in Large-Scale Environments Leveraging Structural Priors from osmAG
上海科技大学.authors_text: Xu Ma, Jiajie Zhang, Fujing Xie, Sören Schwertfeger
上海科技大学.summary: This paper presents a WiFi-based localization method that utilizes OpenStreetMap structural priors to improve robot positioning accuracy in large, GPS-denied environments.
上海科技大学.debug_abstract: WiFi localization offers a lightweight global prior for robots in GPS-denied environments, but fingerprinting requires dense surveys and generalizes poorly beyond surveyed areas. We model received signal strength indicator (RSSI) measurements using OpenStreetMap Area Graph (osmAG) structural priors. Offline, known anchor access points (APs) support sequential calibration of line-of-sight (LOS) propagation and wall attenuation; unknown AP locations are then estimated by alternating ray-wall intersection checks, signal compensation, and least-squares fitting. The resulting AP map supports online robot position estimation using the same structure-aware model. In experiments in an 11,025~m$^2$ multi-floor environment, our method reduces the mean AP localization error from 5.86~m to 3.79~m. Mean robot localization errors are 3.12~m in fingerprinted areas and 3.83~m in unfingerprinted areas, where four baselines yield 11.00--20.21~m. The WiFi-related map representation achieves approximately 251:1 compression relative to the raw fingerprint database. These results support structural modeling for compact global localization beyond surveyed regions. Code and data: https://github.com/XuMa369/osmag-wifi-localization

南方科技大学.title: Navi-Agent: Unlocalized Monocular Navigation Agent
南方科技大学.authors_text: Wenyuan Xie, Mengyang Hong, Yongzhong Wang, Yanbiao Ji, Yijin Zhou
南方科技大学.summary: Navi-Agent is a zero-shot VLN-CE system that utilizes a coordinate-free spatial state from visual observations for effective navigation and task verification in unknown environments.
南方科技大学.debug_abstract: Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires an embodied agent to execute long-horizon instructions in unknown environments. Existing zero-shot VLN-CE systems typically maintain spatial states through geometric localization or coordinate-based representations. Recent geometry-constrained navigation removes depth and globally consistent coordinates, but maintaining persistent spatial awareness for place confirmation, progress verification, and recovery remains challenging. We present Navi-Agent, a zero-shot VLN-CE agent that constructs a coordinate-free spatial state from visual observations and executed motion histories. Navi-Agent organizes this state as a navigation topology, where nodes represent visual places and edges represent motion transitions. This representation enables observation-based approximate self-localization, task progress verification, and visual revisitation-based recovery. Navi-Agent performs closed-loop navigation by decomposing instructions into sub-goals, executing local visual navigation, and verifying visited places through the constructed spatial state. Experiments on zero-shot VLN-CE benchmark and real-world robot platforms show that Navi-Agent achieves state-of-the-art performance among geometry-constrained methods while remaining competitive with approaches relying on geometric localization.

SU Lab.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
SU Lab.authors_text: Yuhan Tang, Ke Fan, Xinkai Zou, Baichuan Mo, Kangxin Cui
SU Lab.summary: The paper introduces Ask2Decide, a benchmark assessing LLM agents' ability to acquire crucial decision-relevant information from humans, revealing significant challenges in planning accuracy.
SU Lab.debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

具身智能研究中心.title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Haofeng Wang, Xuanyi Liu, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang
具身智能研究中心.summary: PhysCapBench is a novel benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, assessing annotation quality across diverse domains to enhance physical AI training and performance.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

具身智能实验室.title: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
具身智能实验室.authors_text: Fengmin Wu, Sicong Liu, Zimu Zhou, Chenren Xu, Wanbing Zhao
具身智能实验室.summary: UbiHearo is a mobile assistant for Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing users that provides scenario-aware sound guidance through a neuro-symbolic approach, enhancing situational awareness and personalized responses.
具身智能实验室.debug_abstract: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. However, existing mobile assistants largely reduce acoustic scenes to isolated labels or generic alerts, failing to provide contextual guidance when the same sound implies different risks across scenarios. We present \sysname, a mobile hearing assistant agent that closes the sensing--reasoning--action loop for \textit{scenario-aware} and \textit{personalized} DHH assistance. \sysname adopts a \textit{neuro-symbolic} design that transforms continuous acoustic and physical context streams into structured intermediate representations (IRs) for controllable reasoning and guidance. It introduces three key mechanisms. \textit{First}, a perception-thresholded sensing mechanism enables energy-efficient always-on awareness by activating processing only for perceptually meaningful events while preserving safety-critical cues through deterministic overrides. \textit{Second}, a staged neuro-symbolic reasoning framework performs promptless scenario understanding by conditioning an on-device audio-language model on structured IRs instead of user-authored context descriptions. \textit{Third}, a bounded human-in-the-loop personalization mechanism adapts user-specific guidance through lightweight on-device decision-boundary updates while preserving population-aligned reasoning. We evaluate \sysname on smartphones and in-vehicle systems across diverse scenarios. It achieves favorable accuracy--latency--energy tradeoffs and personalized guidance.
